ResponsesInList.Title: Important: Please read before posting
ResponsesInList.Text: It's likely that any problem you have found while using the Moodle Mobile app has already been reported and a solution or workaround found. This is why we ask you to do the following before posting in this forum: Check the Moodle Mobile FAQ . If your problem remains unresolved after checking the FAQ, please follow the guide Moodle Mobile debugging WS requests to isolate and report the problem. Finally, try to reproduce the problem on a free MoodleCloud site. You can restore a backup there to check if the issue is solved in the latest Moodle version. Remember that because of privacy laws, we can’t access your site to debug what is happening. Thus, do not share access credentials (with the exception of a MoodleCloud site created for testing purposes only which doesn't contain any private data).

ResponsesInList.Title: Important: Please read before posting
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you for enabling me to be a member of the Moodle forum.

ResponsesInList.Title: Important Updates to Moodle Mobile App Requirements
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everyone, I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to share some upcoming changes in the Moodle mobile app requirements: Mobile app version 4.4 Changes (Expected release date around May): Minimum Android Version: Updated to 7 (from 5.1) Minimum iOS Version: Stays at 11 ; (update June 2024!, minimum will be iOS 13) although it will be only tested in versions iOS 14 onward Note: Android 5 and 6 users (currently a 0.5% of our user base) can still use version 4.3 but won't receive new updates . Mobile app version 4.5 Changes (Expected release date November): Moodle site compatibility: Only for Moodle LMS 3.9 onward Users will be still able to connect to Moodle sites running 3.5.x to 3.8.x, but some functions may be limited. Please notice that we only guarantee that the app will always work with Moodle LMS supported versions, however, we understand the need to support older versions. Why these changes? Compliance: Aligning with app store policies requires the use of the latest library/framework versions, requiring the new Android/iOS minimum versions. Simplification: Updating allows us to reduce maintenance costs given our limited resources. Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Embedded YouTube videos on iOS Moodle App - Error 153
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Ian, Unfortunately recent changes implemented by YouTube have disrupted the functionality of embedded YouTube videos in the Moodle app and other apps. This issue is beyond our control, and we have already reported this problem to all the third-parties that could provide a solution to help address this issue. We are developing a workaround that will be included in the next version of the app, 5.1.0. Please note that the 5.1.0 app is still under development, and it will take some time to complete the quality assurance process and make it available in the app stores. In the interim, we have a couple of recommendations: If you are using the Moodle media filter, please disable it for YouTube. This will display a link instead of an embedded video. However, please be aware that if videos are only linked, then they will not display embedded in LMS. If you have them in an iframe, they will be displayed on LMS. Inform users that they can view the video directly on YouTube by tapping on "Watch video on YouTube". Alternatively if you don’t want to disable the media filter, you can add the following HTML code after each video to display a link in the app (please notice the link will only work on the app, not for the site): `

If the video does not play, please click here ``` `

` We appreciate your understanding and patience as we work to resolve this issue. For more information, we suggest you that become a watcher of that issue ( MOBILE-4924 ), so you will receive automatic updates. Kind regards, Isabel

ResponsesInList.Title: Remove progress bar and % from free Moodle Mobile app?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I've done my best to search for the answer to this one, but we are stuck and it's rather urgent. We need to have Activity Completion in one of our New Student Orientation courses for the Instructors to use behind-the-scenes. We do *not* want the students to see the progress of their course or % on their dashboards. I was able to remove it from the web, but we cannot figure out how to hide it on Moodle. We are on Moodle 3.8 and using the free version of Moodle Mobile 3.9.2. I can see Course completion from this page: Administration / Mobile app / Mobile features and have tried to disable this feature, but I guess I can only do one at a time? And it seems to make no difference. Does anyone have any ideas? Thanks, Bobby

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove progress bar and % from free Moodle Mobile app?
ResponsesInList.Text: I'll add to my post in case this is a better question: We have a site using Restrict Access based upon groups for viewing resources and doing activities . A student in one group is completing all of the available activities, but the course completion is telling them they are not complete. We think this is because that can't get to the content we have prevented them from seeing. Is there a way to have Completion Tracking respect what we have set through Restrict Access? Otherwise, I have to get this progress bar turned off for the students. We used the CSS trick in the browser, but the app is showing it and alarming the students. Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove progress bar and % from free Moodle Mobile app?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bobby, unfortunately the only way to hide the progress bar in the app without changing Moodle core code is with a remote theme (CSS), but that feature is only available for Premium sites. The "Course completion" disabled feature only hides the Course Completion tab in the tabs at the top of the course, but the progress bar is still displayed. It basically hides what in web is displayed in the Course Completion block. In case you're interested, here you'll find more info about the plans: https://apps.moodle.com/local/apps/ Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove progress bar and % from free Moodle Mobile app?
ResponsesInList.Text: For posterity: we finally resolved this by signing up for the Premium app. I created a {moodle root}/local/mobile.css file and referenced it with the mobilecssurl setting. Because there's no real documentation on how to target specific components and the example themes do not discuss the progress bar, I had to repeatedly rename the URL by appending a version hash "#1" "#2" etc to it to keep trying new CSS approaches. It seemed like you also had to log out and back in to see the fresh styles. Finally, this CSS worked: .core-progress-bar progress, .core-progress-text { display: none !important; } I'm not sure how much of that is necessary but this was the first thing that actually worked. The Moodle Mobile Themes doc is useful but doesn't list all the components or how target them with selectors, so I looked at the mobile app's github repo to figure that out.

ResponsesInList.Title: Improvents to support customisations and extend the Moodle mobile app functionality
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everyone, I’d like to share some of the work we’re planning to make it easier for Moodle developers, content creators and site administrators to customise and extend the Moodle mobile app functionality. Our goal is to provide more flexibility for those who want to adapt the app to their specific needs and support customisations already present on your Moodle LMS site. Here’s a summary of the upcoming improvements we’re working on related to site plugins and configuration. For admins and content creators: Support custom user menu items Site administrators will be able to personalise the user account menu by adding their own options. App version 5.2. It will require upgrading to Moodle LMS 5.2 Allow embedding of remote JavaScript content Administrators will be able to configure an allow-list of scripts that can be embedded by teachers and content creators. This will simplify including remote content such as Typeforms, Tweets, or any other interactive elements that require JavaScript. App version 5.2. It will require upgrading to Moodle LMS 5.2 Add data-category-id for better styling Similar to how data-course-id works today, we’ll add data-category-id attributes to relevant elements. This will allow applying different CSS styles per course or category (or even hiding specific elements if needed). App version 5.2. Support for Bootstrap components and helpers Developers and content creators will be able to use Bootstrap 4 and 5 components (tabs, carousels, accordions, modals, collapse, etc.) and Bootstrap CSS helpers directly in the app content. App version 5.1 to be released on November 25 For developers: Extend site plugins capabilities Site plugins will not only be able to add menu items (in the More menu, User menu, or User profile) but also render HTML content in the menu/page itself. This will allow developers to display banners, images, or any other type of information without forcing users to open a new page. App version 5.2. Control the order of main menu tabs Developers will be able to define the preferred order for elements in the main bottom tabs menu, making it easier to adapt navigation to specific use cases. App version 5.2. We’d love to hear your feedback on these upcoming features: - Are there other areas where you’d like more extensibility? - How do you see yourself using these new capabilities in your projects? Thanks, Juan Leyva Product Director, Mobile Solutions

ResponsesInList.Title: Concern Regarding Local Storage of Files and SCREENRECORDING in Moodle Mobile App
ResponsesInList.Text: We are currently using the Moodle application and uploading SCORM packages and other learning materials (such as posters) by storing them in an S3 bucket and serving them directly through Moodle. However, we have observed that when users log in to the Moodle application through our website, the data (SCORM packages and other uploaded files) is being stored locally on the Android device under the following path: /data/com.moodle.moodlemobile/sites/filepool/ This behavior results in the entire content being saved on the user's phone storage. Could you please confirm if this is the default functionality of the Moodle mobile app? If so, is there any configuration or setting available to restrict or disable this local caching behavior, especially for SCORM packages and media files? Second question is can we restrict Screenrecording and Screenshot in moodle application We would like to ensure that sensitive content is not permanently stored on user devices for security and copyright reasons.

ResponsesInList.Title: Concern Regarding Local Storage of Files and SCREENRECORDING in Moodle Mobile App
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Abhishek, Notice that in order to be able to play packages offline, the app will have to download the SCORM zip to the user's device. In order to prevent this behaviour, you can enable the global SCORM setting "Protect package downloads" ( protectpackagedownloads ). Enabling the previous setting will disable the offline mode for the SCORM activity. > Second question is can we restrict Screenrecording and Screenshot in moodle application This can only be achieved by building your own version of the mobile app to be able to change by code this behaviour. Kind regards, Isabel

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: H5P fails on Android Moodle App or browser
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Craig, Please check whether a Proxy/Firewall/Web Server security module is setting the X-Frame-Options header in your HTTP request responses. If this is the case, it is recommended to deactivate this feature as it may cause conflicts, as Moodle already sets this header by default. Please visit the Moodle FAQ - H5P packages don't work on my site Kind regards, Isabel

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: H5P fails on Android Moodle App or browser
ResponsesInList.Text: I literally just fixed my server :D In your root directory (/var/www/html/moodle or wherever your root is) make a file .htaccess. <If Module mod_headers.c> Header always append X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN </IfModule> I run our moodle on our own server on a VPN but I encourage you to read about headers to be on the safe side. The last thing you want to do is make your server vulnerable. Hope this helps and was my solution for my scenario.  Your mileage may very.

ResponsesInList.Title: Mobile 5.0.0 Location services disabled, can anything be done?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Lawrence, unfortunately there were major reasons why this feature had to be removed, the most relevant one that it is not detailed in the tracker issue is that Google Play is enforcing policies to forbid using location in apps addressed to kids in primary education mostly, this raised some warnings in the Google Play console and not removing it was not an option. ResponsesInList.Title: PDF download issue
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello everyone, I have a question about downloading PDF documents in the app. Several users have pointed out to me that whenever they try to open or download a PDF, it is always displayed with a special name, e.g., "Name of PDF_konvertiert_e3ce4e1ff1cfe0cbe882fa7d2a3d2f4e." For proper sorting, the name must always be removed. The problem only occurs in the app and only on Apple devices. Everything is perfectly normal on the website. What could be causing this? Best regards, Andreas

ResponsesInList.Title: PDF download issue
ResponsesInList.Text: Possible Causes: Automatic File Conversion on Apple Devices Apple systems sometimes auto-convert files when downloading or previewing in apps. During this conversion, a hash or suffix like _konvertiert_<hash> may be added to ensure uniqueness or prevent file caching. Improper Handling of Download Headers If the Content-Disposition header is missing or misconfigured, iOS/macOS may generate a random name instead of preserving the original filename. This header tells the system how to name the file on download. In-App Viewer or WebView Behavior If your app uses a custom PDF viewer or embedded browser, it may alter filenames internally when downloading or exporting files. This is especially common if the PDF is processed before download (for example, flattened, annotated, or decrypted). Third-Party Libraries and Rendering Tools Some PDF libraries or plugins generate temporary versions of the document for display, and these can be saved with modified filenames, particularly if file protection is involved. Recommended Fixes: Set the Correct HTTP Headers Ensure your server includes the Content-Disposition header when serving PDFs: `arduino` `Copy` `Edit` Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="YourOriginalFileName.pdf" Disable Automatic Conversion (if applicable) Check if the app is converting PDFs during download. If so, provide an option to disable the conversion or use the original file name in the output. Implement File Rename Logic In your app, especially if built with Swift or React Native, implement logic to rename the downloaded file back to its original name after saving it locally. Additional Tip: Handling Protected PDFs If your PDFs are encrypted or have restrictions, these may interfere with normal rendering and download behavior. In such cases, consider using a tool like SysTools PDF Unlocker , which: Removes user or owner passwords from PDF files Eliminates restrictions on copying, printing, or editing Helps retain the original filename and structure during conversion Works on both Windows and macOS This can be particularly helpful if you're preparing the PDFs before delivering them through the app. Conclusion: This filename issue is most likely related to file conversion or download handling specific to Apple devices. By setting proper download headers, avoiding unnecessary conversions, and optionally unlocking PDFs beforehand using tools like SysTools PDF Unlocker, you can ensure a more consistent and predictable download experience for your users. Let me know if you need help reviewing your app's download or server response configuration.

Anyhoo ... for those that might be reading this thread and having to migrate a site off old host to new host ... a tip ... called the 'host file trick'. Every computer (workstation Mac or PC) as well as servers have a hosts file and typically default rules for DNS lookups are: 1. flies (the hosts file), 2.  local DNS (internal p;rivate DNS or public DNS)  and 3. upstream DNS resolvers. One can migrate a site to new hosting and view with the old fully qualified domain name pointed to the new IP entry in the hosts file. In /etc/ a hosts file - which maps IP addresses with FQDN and a short name. (Macs and Linux - on Windows PC's someplace/something similar) So, you could have made an entry in /etc/hosts for the new IP: address by FQDN (DNS not yet changed) and made sure all worked on newly hosted IP server like so: xx.xx.xx.xx hostname.tld.domain shortcutname Non-existing fictcious example: 192.168.1.244 dev.tcea.org dev No need to reboot server ... moodle on new hosting already knows it's dev.tcea.org (config.php flie entry) ... and your local machine/browser will see dev.tcea.org as that iP address if hosts file not it's true DNS IPv4 assigned to it in DNS which might something like 208.211.xx.xx. If using letsencrypt, those files from old server were probably not xferred to new, so the setup of letsncrypt by the same fqdn might still be required - and one may not need a $ cert. Yes, none of the above is documented in moodle docs migrations ... it's just one of those things that's too complicated to document and one is expected to know quite a bit about hosting. Anyhoo ... 2 addtional cents! 'SoS', Ken And if you are wondering if I have practiced what I preach ... yes, many times.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle Mobile app with self-signed certificate on iOS and Android
ResponsesInList.Text: Asking the question first. There is a lot of background involved that follows the question Does Moodle mobile app have any known issues with a self-signed certificate based HTTPS? Here is what I find: iOS - I have a Moodle setup with a self-signed public/private key pair. It works fine on the desktop browser (after I accept the risk and continue). On the phone, I installed the public key on the iOS device as a trusted certificate following the usual Apple steps. Then safari/ firefox browsers on the phone are readily able to connect to the Moodle server without warnings. But the mobile app fails to connect, it does not even seem to recognize the Moodle server host - (it says it cannot find the server, which I think is misleading because changing only the protocol to HTTP works and connect to the site using the same URL on the mobile browser works. The mobile app error popup says " servernotfound ".) Android : Android does not allow apps to connect using a self-signed certificate unless the certificate is declared within the app (network config xml ) and the certificate is bundled with the app apk file. I made a custom build of the android APK bundling the public certificate, and this too fails like iOS. Again, like iOS, the mobile browser chrome is able to connect to the server once I say OK to the risk. So, it appears it is the app which has a problem. I understand this is an exceptional use case, so I am wondering if there are known issues with this use case. I feel iOS at least should work out of the box since Apple does not have the same intrusive requirements as Android. Why am I trying to achieve this exceptional use case: Background: I have successfully set up Moodle in a school in the local school district that I work with (I work for a Non profit in Education in India). Language teachers use Moodle audio recording activities (via the Atto editor) for spoken language practice. Since Atto editor uses RecordRTC (WebRTC), a HTTPS connection is mandatory. The school district setup does not allow them to have domain names, so I cannot get valid CA signed certificate against a domain. I have installed a self-signed certificate in the Moodle installation. The HTTPS based setup works fine on the desktop browser as well as the mobile browser. The mobile app fails however (as detailed above). Any help is much appreciated ! Using the mobile app and recording in the app will immensely help the teacher community do spoken activities in a more scaleable manner as opposed to desktop. Regards, Chandra

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle Mobile app with self-signed certificate on iOS and Android
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chandra, it is a complex topic, there are several reasons why this won't work out of the box in our app (is not a fault of the app, it is how it was designed by Android and iOS engineers). Why it works in browsers but not in Cordova: In browsers , you can install a root CA in your OS, and the browser will trust certificates issued by that CA. In Cordova apps , especially those using WebView-based networking (e.g., `fetch` , `HttpClient` ), the WebView’s networking stack does not honor user-installed certificates by default. Android (7.0+) added strict rules: apps no longer trust user-installed certificates unless explicitly configured. iOS similarly requires manual handling if you want to trust custom certs. Workaround (Android only): Use a network_security_config.xml (check Android docs for this), chatGPT can provide detailed instructions for a Cordova app like ours On iOS, there’s no way to make a Cordova WebView trust user-installed certs without implementing custom native code to override NSURLSession behavior—which is complex and not recommended. Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Mobile app usage
ResponsesInList.Text:
I am creating some SQL queries to find out about Moodle mobile app usage. There is a table called user_devices that records information from the app and includes a lastmodified column. It looks like the mobile token will by default expire every 12 weeks. So a query on records that have been updated in the last year will typically indicate that a user has used the app at least once in that period. Combining that with lastlogin data from the user table should give a finer grain of information.

I am currently working with this query to count the numbers of “logins” using the mobile app over the last 12 months (or settable period of time), using report_customsql

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ud.userid) AS users_who_have_logged_in
FROM {user_devices} ud
JOIN {user} u ON u.id = ud.userid
WHERE u.lastlogin >= :since_lastlogin_date
AND ud.timemodified >= :since_timemodified_date

All feedback is greatly appreciated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SSO failing on Android Moodle 4.0.1, ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, that error is displayed when Android doesn't have any app to handle the URL scheme (in this case, "moodlemobile"). If the Moodle app from Google Play is installed in the device, this error shouldn't appear. If you have the app installed, can you try to uninstall it and install it again? Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: SSO failing on Android Moodle 4.0.1, ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME
ResponsesInList.Text: The error message ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME is seen on SSO failing on Android Moodle 4.0.1. It is a browser-related problem that appears when the browser is able to process a URL that it simply doesn’t know how to handle. URL scheme is the first element of a URL that defines the protocol that is necessary. The error can be triggered by several factors, which can be broadly categorized into issues related to custom URL schemes, browser compatibility, extensions, and typos. I hope it helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle app offline content - LMS upgrade
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Victor, There are a few things to consider here: Users will have to pre- download in advance the course materials they want to access offline The offline mode in the app is enabled only when the app detects that the phone does not have an internet connection. If you site is down for maintenance, I'm not sure how the app will behave, as the "offline mode" is for when the user device is offline, not when the remote system is offline Considering the previous, it won't be a smooth experience for your users.. You will need to let them know to prepare in advance and provide instructions to activate the offline mode by putting their phones in airplane mode or similar. And, of course, we'd recommend to test this in advance with a staging site Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Accessibility of the free mobile app
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Alexander, Please let me clarify how this works. Firstly, this is not new; it started around 5 years ago ( see original announcement ), but we have been enforcing it lately by adding additional providers. It is affecting less than 1% of the Moodle sites using the Moodle mobile app, and we do not expect this percentage to change in the following years. This is only affecting sites hosted by companies that specialise in Moodle LMS hosting, which are not Moodle Partners. This is NOT affecting organisations using generic hosting providers, organisations using their own infrastructure or organisations that are hosting with companies that are not direct competitors of Moodle partners. As you can imagine, it is becoming more and more expensive in all aspects to be competitive and maintain our very complex products. Finally, this is quite difficult to communicate as we cannot directly mention all the non-official Moodle hosting providers affected by this by name. As I said before, we tried to contact all of them in advance (6 months) using their contact email addresses so they were aware and could plan to provide alternative solutions to their customers. Some of the challenges we encountered include: 1. Question types used from plugins, are not always supported in the Moodle app, therefore we encouraged students to rather complete quizzes in their browsers and not the mobile app. This caused students to mostly just use their mobile device browsers and not the app. 2. Maintainability of a custom branded app is a bit of a challenge, where a progressive web app will "always" be up to date, due to basically being a browser-wrapper in app form. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Progressive web app vs Moodle Mobile App
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jaco, I recently viewed a presentation about this, https://assets.moodlemoot.org/sites/77/20180704162809/Day2_DRAFT_turning_moodle_pwa.pdf You could technically do it, but it will be a LOT of work and apart from that: - You won't be able to do the intensive caching the app does - It won't work offline as the app does (for example, SCORM module downloads and unzip the package for offline) - You won't be able to download complete courses/ sections for offline - Push notifications will stop working (you will have to implement your own solution) - Same for local notifications, you will have to create your own implementation - Some functionalities will behave differently, like opening files directly with the native app And I suppose there will be more issues...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to set fixed site url?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Zonair, All your changes to the app functionality should be made in the src folder. For setting a static site url (and thereby going directly to the login screen) you have to edit the src\configconstants.ts file. More specificially you should enter you site url in: static siteurl = ''; This is also the file where you can set the default language, site name (displayed inside the app) and other things. Basically this file contains all the same parameters as src\config.json . ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to set fixed site url?
ResponsesInList.Text: > PS. does anyone know what the purpose of config.json is, since changes here are not reflected, and since I managed to compile a perfectly working (except push notifications) customized app without touching src/config.json? The `config.json` file is the one you should be modifying, there is a gulp task that generates `src/configconstants.ts` reading this json file. If you place your modifications in the typescript file you risk losing them, because that file is not tracked in the repository and it can be overwritten if some script regenerates it. You can regenerate it yourself by calling the gulp task named `config` , for example doing `npx gulp` .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Automatically open hyperlinks in Moodle App
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Richard, if the link is clicked inside the Moodle app, the app will always try to open it inside the app (if the feature is supported). You don't need to do anything special in there, just use a regular link like you do in laptop. It gets trickier in mobile browsers. You can use a custom URL scheme to launch the app from the browser as it's explained in this guide . However, as far as I know clicking this link in a laptop won't do anything. And I think the same happens if the app is not installed, I think it won't open the Google Play / App Store (but you might want to verify this). The first problem (laptop) can probably be fixed with a custom Moodle filter to use the normal link or the custom URL scheme depending on the device. So teachers can use regular links and then your filter can replace them with the app URL scheme format if you detect that the user agent belongs to a mobile browser. As for opening Google Play / App Store, if it's not opened automatically then you might have to add a second link to open the store, but it's not a good solution in terms of UX. Maybe there are better solutions, I don't know much about that part. Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Wert, I'm not an expert in this area so I might be wrong, but as far as I know in order to do that an app needs to declare in the app's manifest the domains (URLs) that wants to open, it's not something done dynamically. Since the Moodle app is used to connect to any Moodle site it's not feasible to support this, since we'd need to declare in our manifest the URLs of all the Moodle sites out there. ResponsesInList.Title: Alternative solution with webservice token in scorm
ResponsesInList.Text: Solved ! I want to thank Dani of Moodle App team 🤩, and share with you his answer. We only use the script in content rendered by the app, content rendered in an iframe is not treated. That's why it works in Page (the app replaces the original Vimeo link and uses the wsplayer.php script instead), but it's not working for SCORM because the SCORM content is rendered in an iframe. What we always recommend in cases like this is to contact Vimeo and ask them to support restricting videos by user agent too, not just by URL . That way you could configure the video to work in the app. Hopefully if they keep getting requests like this they might implement it in the future. If the client doesn't want to make the videos public, the only solution I can think of is that you edit the SCORM package and manually replace the links to Vimeo to use the wsplayer.php instead. This wsplayer script requires the video ID and a user token (to make sure that only users authenticated in the site can view the video), so you should create a new user that isn't enrolled to any course or anything (because his token can be used to call any WebService), create a WebService token for this user and then use it in the SCORM. The URLs to the site will need to be hardcoded, so this SCORM will only work for a specific site. E.g. if the SCORM has an iframe pointing to https://player.vimeo.com/video/VIDEOID , you should replace the URL with YOURSITEURL/media/player/vimeo/wsplayer.php?video=VIDEOID&token=TOKEN The solution is quite ugly, but it's the only one I can think of.

ResponsesInList.Title: Problems with My Courses list
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Moodlers We are experiencing some issues with the Moodle mobile app. The error is random and occurs in less than 1% of users (students account) using the mobile app, regardless of the operating system (iOS: moodle mobile 4.5.0&ipados 18.1.1 or Android). LMS Moodle version 4.1.9 Users report problems loading the My Courses list. The error message displayed is: Error connecting to the server : Http failure response for https://our_moodle_url/webservice/rest/server.php?moodlewsrestformat=json&wsfunction=core_enrol_get_users_courses: 0 Unknown Error In the logs, we noticed that for some users/at random moments, the My Courses list is retrieved using the function `core_enrol_get_users_courses` , while for others it is retrieved using `core_course_get_courses_by_field` (in this case, the error does not occur). What determines which function is called, and why does the first one return an error?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problems with My Courses list
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, both web services are used to retrieve information about the course, core_enrol_get_users_courses it is usually used when we need to show a list of courses before accessing. to them and the other one in case we need additional data depending on your site configuration before accessing a course or just when you access a course. The Error connecting to the server errors are problems with your web server, it seems that the HTTP requests are failing from the PHP side of things, I'd recommend to check the web server or PHP logs to understand what could be causing the issues, and, if you can, temporary disable all the plugins you have installed that might cause issues at course level.

ResponsesInList.Title: Shared files
ResponsesInList.Text: How is the Shared files (under three dots, App settings in the mobile app) used? I found documentation online that says you can share a file from your device to the app and it will be stored there. However when I do that, nothing appears in Shared files. Also, there is no Add/+ button in the Shared files interface to directly upload files to this location. Is this an on-device only resource? How does one put/get files from it? Thanks in advance!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Shared files
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Michelle, files shared with the app are linked to a certain user. If you don't have any user stored in the app, when you share a file with the app you should see a toast explaining this. If you only have 1 user stored in the app, sharing the file will automatically link it to the user account in the app. After doing it you should see a "Success" modal: If you have several users/sites, when sharing the file you will be asked which user you want to link the file to. After sharing the file with the app, if you go to the Shared files option in the app you should be able to see it. If you have several users/sites: Opening "User menu (avatar) > Preferences > Shared files" will only display the files linked to the current user. Opening "More tab (3 dots) > App Settings > Shared files" will display a drop-down selector where you can select which user you want to see. Here's a screenshot of how it looks like: Please notice these files are only stored in the app, they aren't uploaded in Moodle LMS unless you use them later in an activity, private files, etc. If this isn't working for you, can you please let us know how are you sharing the file with the app and if the app displays any message? E.g. here's a screenshot of how I share a file with the app, from Safari: Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle app security
ResponsesInList.Text: That's not quite correct..  airnotifier does not send the notification directly to the mobile device. It sends the notification to Google and Apple servers which then send it to the mobile device. Hosting your own airnotifier server is possible but all that does is remove Moodle HQ's server from the equation, it does not eliminate Google or Apple servers from the process. If you're concerned about this, the best option is to enable encryption for messaging.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle app security
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, the only time messages/content travel through external servers is when you have enabled Push Notifications for mobile devices which is optional. In that case, when a Push notification (such as a notification about a new post, private message, etc...) is going to be sent to a user , it will firstly go through Moodle Airnotifier server, then through Google/Apple servers and it finally will arrive to the end user. But even with Push Notifications enabled, you can choose the option for end-to-end encryption of all communications, so nothing will travel "in plan text/clear" through Moodle and Google/Apple notifications servers. You have more information here: https://docs.moodle.org/en/Moodle_app_notifications#For_administrators and in the Section within Schedule 1 of our Data Processing Agreement (DPA), which can be accessed through the following link: https://moodle.com/privacy-notice/ Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Clarification about Moodle App Policy Changes for Free Users
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Job, Restrictions will only apply to Moodle sites that are hosted by non-official Moodle LMS service providers (companies offering Moodle hosting services that are not Moodle Certified Partners). The majority of sites are not affected by this, as most organizations use their own means, MoodleCloud , Moodle Partners services, or generic PHP hosting providers. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle APP + Vimeo privacy setting
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Kristian, We used to suggest using X-Frame-Options "ALLOW-FROM *" , but someone from the community told me that it didn't work for him: "It turned out that’s not the 100% correct syntax and some Firefox started to behave badly (didn’t display iFrames from the Kaltura SaaS plugin any more). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle APP + Vimeo privacy setting
ResponsesInList.Text: Ok, we've been reviewing this and we've updated the Moodle app FAQs . In Moodle 3.7 and higher it's no longer needed to enable the Moodle setting "Allow frame embedding" to make Vimeo videos work in the Moodle app, because it no longer applies to requests coming from the app. You just need to be sure that your server does NOT set the X-Frame-Options header. If you want it to be set to "sameorigin" then you should just enable disable the "Allow frame embedding setting in Moodle instead. Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Inapp browser auto-login moodle mobile 3.2
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Devendiran, there are some restrictions to make auto-login work: The Moodle site needs to be 3.2 or higher. It doesn't work in previous Moodle sites. Your site needs to use SSL (https). After fulfilling the previous conditions, you should invalidate all tokens so the users create a new one. I think the easiest way is to go to the external_tokens table in your Moodle database and modify the value of " validuntil ". Also, please take into account that a certain user can only auto-login every 6 minutes (for security reasons). Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Inapp browser auto-login moodle mobile 3.2
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Devendiran, the in-app browser and the system browser use a different session. This means that authenticating in one of them won't affect the other. If you auto-login in in-app browser you'll have to wait 6 minutes to be able to auto-login in the system browser. Once authenticated in the system browser, the session should be kept for future requests. Also, we detected that in some devices the in-app browser session is resetted when it's closed, so in that case the auto-login will only work once every 6 minutes in in-app browser. Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Inapp browser auto-login moodle mobile 3.2
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, when you create a custom menu item you have 3 options: browser: the page is opened in the system's browser (Chrome, Safari, Firefox , ...). inappbrowser: the page is opened in a "popup" (browser embedded in the app). The app opens a new window, like a popup, inside the app itself. You need to close this inappbrowser to be able to use the app again since it overlays the whole app. embedded: the page is opened inside the app itself, using an iframe. This is not a browser, it's similar to opening a SCORM . The first 2 options, browser and inappbrowser, support auto-login. The third one, embedded, doesn't support it right now, we have an open issue to fix it: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MOBILE-2161 Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Accidentally shared personal file to Moodle App (IOS), where do they go?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris, The file isn't uploaded automatically to the Moodle site, it's only in your device. The file should be on 'Shared files' on the Moodle app. That is an internal folder, you are the only one that can access to it. You can access this folder by tapping on the three horizontal dots icon, tapping on 'App settings', and then tapping on 'Shared files'. You can delete the files there. Take into account that while confirming this behaviour, our team detected that there is a combination where the file is not send anywhere. ResponsesInList.Title: How to keep the app offline?
ResponsesInList.Text: dear Moodlers, THE QUESTION is it possible to force the Moodle app to be offline and stay offline (despite device is having internet connection), and go online only at the time the user say so? CONTEXT / BACKGROUND INFORMATION for a running project in rural Ethiopia (time of writing: April 2024), we prepared 55 units of Android powered tablets with Moodle and a course downloaded. Note that these tablets are not rooted. To prep these 55 units, we have done the whole 9-yards: unpacked, charged, do the onboarding, login using a user from Google Workspace --specially setup for this purpose, go to play store, installed Moodle (MDM does not push the app fast enough), logged in to Moodle, and finally downloaded the course. The idea of this whole ordeal is that the infrastructure is just not sufficient to have the users connected --speed, infrastructure, costs, etc. So we prep everything in a location where the internet is strong, fast, and stable, with the idea that the app will facilitate the learning activities offline. Apart from Moodle, we also installed another app to enable the monitoring of pregnancy and newborn. This second app would need to be connected from time to time to send the recorded data back to the server . After the tablets shipped and distributed in the most rural parts of Ethiopia, an in-country representative come visiting to check on the progress between now and then. He carries a mobile pocket WiFi with him to enable the second app to connect and send the data. BUT...the kicker is: the Moodle app also sees that "ooooh, there's a connection, lemme update my stuffs". And there goes all the hardwork of prepping the Moodle to be offline, because when the Moodle app updates the activities and the connection is severed, the previously downloaded materials are gone, and thus makes the activity unusable. I have read in the documentation about the app https://docs.moodle.org/403/en/Moodle_app_synchronization , but I am afraid this is not enough in the sense that if the tablet is connected with WiFi, it will call home --the option to kill the app is might be too technical; we are dealing with a very diverse level of tech-literacy. So... any tips on keeping the moodle app offline, until we / the user manually trigger otherwise? TIA !

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how to access to offline file path to play video? (Developer problem)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I see you're adding the core-external-content directive to the "source", that directive should try to download the file in the following cases: If the size of the file is less than 20MB and the user is on WiFi, or if the file less than 2MB, it should be downloaded the first time it's rendered. If the file is bigger than that and the user is on WiFi, it should be downloaded in background the first time the user plays it. Please check that you fulfill any of those conditions. In the directive core-format-text we apply core-external-content automatically to all media elements, and in case of "source" elements we convert the "src" to "target-src", I guess we found a problem when using "src" directly (probably the video didn't detect the change of URL ). So if the video is not downloaded, you can try using [targetSrc]="'<% urlout %>'" instead of src (please notice there are single quotes inside double quotes. If this still doesn't work, you can try debugging the core-external-content directive to see why it isn't downloading the file. Or you can also try using core-format-text , but that means converting the video HTML to a string so it's better if core-external-content works properly without doing this. Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how to access to offline file path to play video? (Developer problem)
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi sadaf, one possible solution could be to use a URL in the app that downloads the decoded file already, so the file stored in the app wouldn't need to be decoded. But maybe you don't want to do that for security/privacy reasons. The first thing you need is the local path of the file, and you can obtain it using the CoreFilepoolProvider service in the Javascript code returned along with the template, in your classes/output/mobile.php. For example, you can use: 
```text
const url = 'THE URL OF THE FILE'; // If you don't have this URL in JS code, you can pass it to JS using otherdata and this.CONTENT_OTHERDATA.
```
 
```text
const path = await this.CoreFilepoolProvider.getFilePathByUrl(this.CoreSitesProvider.getCurrentSiteId(), url);
```
 With this code you will have the path of the file. Please notice that the file needs to be downloaded, if the file isn't downloaded you should either use the online URL or you can force downloading the file using 
```text
this.CoreFilepoolProvider.downloadUrl(this.CoreSitesProvider.getCurrentSiteId(), url)
```
 This function will download the file if needed, and then return the path. Once you have the path, you can read the file. Maybe the fetch function will work for local files too, but we usually use: 
```text
this.CoreFileProvider.readFile(path, format);
```
 Where format is 0 for text, 1 for data URL, 2 for binary string and 3 for array buffer. Looking at your code, I guess you want to use format=3. I hope this helps. Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: File saying its been uploaded later than i uploaded it (urgent!)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Orian, This forum is typically used by people responsible for managing Moodle in learning organizations. Students typically reach out to the designated person or team at your school or learning organization, who then conduct an investigation and use this forum accordingly. We don’t have access to your school’s Moodle site, your user information, or the configuration of your school’s Moodle site so we don't have context . In the event of server -related issues while a student is attempting to upload a file for an assignment on the Moodle app, if the app is unable to connect to the server the attempt will be saved offline for later synchronisation. Similarly, if there are device-related issues during the file upload process, the attempt will be saved offline for later synchronisation. In such cases, a warning message in dark yellow will appear, indicating that the assignment contains offline data that needs to be synchronised. Could you please clarify if you were attempting to upload a file to an assignment activity? (There are several locations were you could be uploading a file, such as a quiz, a forum, some plugins, ...) Additionally, could you provide screenshots of the activity in question? This will allow us to review important details such as open and due dates, submission status, and any other available information. With that information we will test the app in case there is an issue on the app. Please be aware that we are a small team and our capacity is currently limited due to the holidays. Thank you for your understanding. Best regards, Isabel

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Orian, We've conducted various tests, and when a file fails to upload to the server, a screen message confirms pending data synchronisation (" This Assignment has offline data to be synchronised "). Additionally, automatic uploads occur seamlessly with an active connection, without delays. No complaints regarding similar issues have been reported over the years. There are multiple potential reasons for failed uploads: Internet connectivity issues Server downtime Server slow response Script errors handling uploads on the server side Another possibility is server-level antivirus plugins blocking uploads until scanned. If you're certain you didn't encounter the synchronisation message, please inform your IT department to investigate potential errors in the server or the "webservice/upload.php" script used by the app for file transfers. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: תשובה ל: Re: תשובה ל: Re: File saying its been uploaded later than i uploaded it (urgent!)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Orian, yes, a problem in the server can also cause the file upload to be delayed. For example, if the server is down and the app is unable to connect, then the app stores the file and information to be sent later automatically, and displays the yellow box you can see in Isabel's last post. The app will retry the upload in several minutes (15 minutes approx, although this time can change depending on several conditions), but the app needs to be running in order to upload the file: in Android it can be running in background, but in iOS it needs to be in foreground to be able to upload the file. If you closed the app or Android killed it to save battery, then the file won't be uploaded until the app is opened again. Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Cannot Use the Moodle App in a browser
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Marcus, That finally worked! Here are the details... for a Windows 11 user. 0.- On your Windows box at the root (or anywhere else) create a new directory which will be used by Chromium to store data (to avoid the error message " Google Chrome cannot read and write to its data directory :") Call it, e.g. c:\moodleapp After installing Chromium-Canary, go to the Google Chrome Canary shortcut on your Windows desktop and right-click Properties. In the Target field, it says "C:\Users\josep\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome SxS\Application\chrome.exe". Of course user will be a different name from "josep". Immediately after "C:\Users\josep\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome SxS\Application\chrome.exe", enter a space and this: --allow-file-access-from-files --disable-web-security --user-data-dir=c:\moodapp -allow-running-insecure-content master.apps.moodledemo.net Done! Now when you click that Google Chrome Canary shortcut on your Windows desktop you are taken to Moodle App demo where you can enter your Moodle site URL, then log in, etc. When Chrome Canary is launched you will see this warning " You are using an unsupported command-line flag: —disable-web-security. Stability and security will suffer." Disregard it. The very first time you launch it the Moodle App Demo site will take some time to appear, this is because Chrome is writing a number of files in your user-data-dir=c:\moodapp as defined previously. The following connections will be much faster. Can someone update the doc at https://moodledev.io/general/app/development/setup/app-in-browser to make it more current?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Language selector missing in Moodle app
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bjørn, let me explain how the multi-lang works in the app (the one in Moodle core, I guess the V2 will be the same but this is a 3rd party plugin so I might be wrong). Most of the content retrieved by the app is filtered at server side, before the app receives the content. That means the app will only receive the text in the "final" language, not all the languages. By default this filtering will use the language selected by the user in LMS (the selector you sent), but the Moodle app sends Moodle a parameter to indicate which language to use instead of the one selected by the user. The language sent by the app is the one selected in App settings. Please notice that the Moodle app has a cache system to decrease the network usage. The Moodle app stores most of the content received from LMS and it won't request it again in a while. This means that the following can happen: A user has the app configured in English. The user opens a course in the app and sees a certain multi-lang content in English. The user goes to App settings and changes the language to German. The user opens the same content again. The app displays the content already stored in the app, so the multi-lang is still displayed in English. If the user performs a "Pull to refresh", the app will re-fetch the data from the server and now the content should be in German. Can you please check if this is your case and it works fine after performing a Pull to refresh? If it still doesn't work, can you please tell me your Moodle version and where do you have those multi-lang texts? E.g. a section description, a book, etc. Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How can I create Moodle App only content?
ResponsesInList.Text: I couldn't find any javascript that worked but settled on a combined CSS approach. For anyone who stumbles on this, here's how I did it. Create two blocks of content served up by the same HTML area/page/block. One chunk of content for web browsers and the other with specific ionic elements. In the MoodleApp only chunk (ionic elements), apply the classes d-bock and d-md-none. This keeps the ionic elements from displaying when viewing through normal browsers. Example: <div id="ionic-grid" class="d-block d-md-none"> In the web browser chuck, apply a class of "mobileapp-excluded". You'll have to create this class in the custom CSS (next step) for the Mobile App (custom CSS / Remote Themes only available for paid customers). Example: <div id="bootstrap-grid" class="mobileapp-excluded"> Create a new rule in the Custom CSS file that hides anything with the "mobileapp-excluded" class. /* This CSS rule will hide an element within the Moodle Mobile App */ .mobileapp-excluded {display: none !important;} Don't forget to refresh your cached CSS on the app (force synchronize the app to grab updated CSS) Before you tell me I'm a fibber: in my testing, the Chromium app often doesn't accurately represent reality within the NativeApps and shows both of the content chunks (seems to ignore my CSS style?). At any rate, in my limited testing, this appears to work and hopefully helps the next person who's asked to deploy MoodleApp only content.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Fatal error building moodle app on iOS. File not found push plugin error.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, that issue was closed because this is not a bug in the app, the app compiles fine. This is only a problem when creating custom apps, and we're currently looking for a way to improve this. As a workaround, you can either edit the Encryption Handler file and change the word "Moodle" by your project's name (e.g. #import "MyProject-Swift.h"), or you can go to Xcode build settings and change the value of "Objective - Generated Interface Header Name" to "Moodle-Swift.h". Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Fatal error building moodle app on iOS. File not found push plugin error.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Aldo, sorry for the delay in answering, I was on annual leave. The fact that there is a workaround decreased the priority of this issue, so we are not working on it right now since we have other issues with higher priority. For the record, in our process of creating BMAs we fixed it by adding the following value in platforms/ios/cordova/build-debug.xcconfig and platforms/ios/cordova/build-release.xcconfig: SWIFT_OBJC_INTERFACE_HEADER_NAME = Moodle-Swift.h This will automatically set the XCode variable to Moodle-Swift and the app should compile fine. Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, if you enable debugging in the site you should be able to get more information. As admin, login in browser and go to "Site administration > Development > Debugging" and set "Debug messages" to DEVELOPER. I recommend to leave "Display debug messages" disabled , otherwise users will see errors and warnings in the UI. After this change, open the Moodle app and go to the "More" page (the 3 dots) > App settings > General and enable "Display debug messages" in there. Now try opening the Dashboard or Home page again, you should now see which field is the one returning an invalid value. Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Text: Fixed: It turns out Moodle block every port except port 443 and 80 and Airnotifier runs on port 8801 so you cannot connect to Airnotifier. I simple fix is allow port 8801 in Moodle Site admin > Security > HTTP Security then add port 8801 to cURL allowed ports list Done!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Please explain me, a non-App person, the limitations of the Moodle App!
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, my replies bellow your questions: Q1. What is a "push notification"? In the Web version Moodle sends forum notifications and also Moodlle messages are mailed to off-line users. Are they "push notifications" or is it something else? Push notifications are alerts/messages received by your phone even when the targeted app for the notification is not open, when you click on it, it will open the app and redirect you to the proper message. For example, if you use private messaging ( whatsapp, telegram, etc..) is when you receive a notification with a new message that someone sent you. Let's say an *educational* institution puts up a Moodle LMS. a) Assume not a single one of its users have Moodle App on their mobile so far. Q2. Can all of them, independent of the number, connect to that Moodle via the App? Specifically, can they use the off-line features like writing forum posts, submitting assignments, answer properly configured quizzes? They get mail notifications from the forum and messaging in Moodle? Yes, they can use the offline features. There are no restrictions for the number of users that can use the app, the only restriction applies to the number of users that can receive Push notifications (alerts from the site) . The only restrictions offline will be downloading complete courses at once with a single click. b) Now assume some of those users need to access other Moodle sites using the Mobile App. Q3. I believe they can store a number of sites (logins) stored in the App and hop between them. What is the limit of that number? There are no limits to the number of logins you can have in the app Q 4. How far does the branding go? Notice that this is an educational institution. Not interested in branding, other than no third party products or links on the App. Mentioning Moodle and links to moodle.org are OK. You can sign up for free at apps.moodle.com to see the branding tool . Y ou can use it for free to see how it would look but it won't apply to your app until you purchase a Premium subscription Hope it clarifies your questions

ResponsesInList.Title: Add referrer URL in Moodle Mobile, hotlinking protection
ResponsesInList.Text: New moodler here and despite searching the vast forum I have a question that I didn't find an answer to. To save moodlecloud disk space and increase performance I have placed videos in my course on the content delivery platform Bunny . To access the media files stored at Bunny I provide a link to the media file at Bunny. Here is an sample URL file.mp4 When I go into the course as a student using the web browser, Bunny detects that my site at moodlecloud is the referrer. That is good because then I can enable hotlink protection in Bunny, so that the files can only be access from the course. If you copy the URL and put it into a browser, you get a "403 forbidden" from Bunny. But this doesn't work with the moodle app (version 4.2.0). The app shows no referrer URL at Bunny. The result from this is that hotlink protection doesn't work with the app.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Add referrer URL in Moodle Mobile, hotlinking protection
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Per, a long time ago we found the same issue with Vimeo. Since Vimeo is an existing media player plugin in LMS we implemented a solution for Vimeo only (it was done in MDL-60264 ): When the app finds an iframe pointing to a Vimeo video, the app replaces the URL to use a script inside LMS . This PHP script basically authenticates the user and displays an iframe with the video. Since the request to Vimeo comes from the Moodle site, the video loads fine (the referrer is the site, not the app). i guess you could implement your own plugin to do something similar. You can implement a script similar to wsplayer (but using Bunny instead), and then create a Text filter plugin to replace the iframes in the app. T he latter is recommended to do it from the app's side, adding mobile support to your text filter plugin (see this guide ). You could also support it from PHP side, checking if the user is accessing through WebServices, but that means you would need to return the user's token in WS responses and that's insecure. We'll talk about this internally to see if we can find an easier way to support other video platforms. Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: CORS issue on moodle mobile app
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, currently there are several places in Moodle where '*' is already used: the WebServices layer, login/token.php, the upload files endpoint, etc. Obviously, making things more limited is usually more secure, but IMO using '*' by itself doesn't have to be a huge risk. IMO it's far more important that you protect any private information requiring a user token or similar like Moodle does. Also, AFAIK there are a lot of public APIs using '*'. Depending on what you're trying to achieve, maybe you prefer to create a new WebService to be called from your mobile API instead of a standalone script. That way the WebService will receive the user token and can decide which information to return based on the user. Cheers, Dani

I will put in what our issue was, how we found it, and how we fixed for future reference of others: 1) Turn on Web Services in Moodle. 2) Turn on Developer level debugging. 3) Wrote the attached script, that uses the MDL API in in Python. (In python execute to install needed modules: pip install requests panda openpyxl ) 4) Then got a useful error message.... FINALLY.  See below for our error.  (The app generically says "Invalid response value detected" ) 5) Fixed to odd values that had somehow entered the database and was throwing the error. A '-1' was under mdl_course.enablecompletion in two courses. Values of 0 or 1 are expected. Boom, worked immediately in the default Moodle App. Our other hard to run down point was the error only showed up if one of these two courses were in the students current enrollments. Unexpected response structure: {'exception': 'invalid_response_exception', 'errorcode': 'invalidresponse', 'message': 'Invalid response value detected', 'debuginfo': 'enablecompletion => Invalid response value detected: Invalid external api response: the value is "-1" of PHP type "string", the server was expecting "bool" type'} Thanks Ken.... ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodlebox and Moodle Mobile App
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi there, sorry for being late to this conversation. This is a recurrent topic, allowing the app to connect to sites using self-signed certificates. Unfortunately, this is not something we can enable/allow in the app that is published in Google Play or the Apple App store, it will open the door to several possible security attacks and it will come also with a rejection for publication in those stores. Please note that a mobile app is not a browser and it does not follow the same rules regarding self-signed certificated. Even for hybrid apps like ours the previous applies. There is a specific mention of this here: https://cordova.apache.org/docs/en/latest/guide/appdev/security/ There are two workarounds here: * Add a switch to MoodleBox so SSL is completely disabled for being able to use the Moodle App * Build your own MoodleBox app, allowing self-signed certificates and adding additional security mechanisms so it only can connect to MoodleBox sites, but you won't be able to publish this app in the stores (you will have to distribute the Android apk or do internal distribution via the Apple App store I hope this clarifies this issue Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodlebox and Moodle Mobile App
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ralf The original MoodleBox comes as http://moodlebox.home/ (no HTTPS). So those who have been using https://moodlebox.home/ (HTTPS) must have made the transition to HTTPS. It is their choice. They can keep HTTPS, can't they? The good news is that, the Moodle Mobile App does not force HTTPS. So http://moodlebox.home/ (no HTTPS) will work even on the Moodle Mobile App, provided that HTTPS is disabled in the MoodleBox (by commenting out the four lines in the Nginx configuration https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=424353#p1739474 and https://discuss.moodlebox.net/d/254-mobile-app/19 , as you've discovered). @Nicolas, what do you think about delivering the MoodleBox with those four lines commented out? It will still work as http://moodlebox.home/ as documented. In the documentation on how to go for HTTPS, mention that those lines need to be uncommented. Kind of logical to me: to go from HTTP to HTTPS both the web server and the application need to be reconfigured. Since the Nginx in MoodleBox is dedicated to this single application, nobody else will be disturbed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: SElinux probable culprit for lack of access to mobile app
ResponsesInList.Text: Besides being 'free', the 'good' thing about letsencrypt is that it is automated. The *bad* thing about letsencrypt is the same thing! This is what that checker site showed ... 2 subdomains for your site and the second doesn't exist. lms.ecoleinternationalethestars.com www.lms.ecoleinternationalethestars.com Below is the bot (acme-challenge) ... _acme-challenge. www.lms.ecoleinternationalethestars.com Name Error - The domain name does not exist Now using a browser, not the moodle app, it can handle the auto forwrd from www.lms.ecoleinternationalethestars.com to just lms.ecoleinternationalethestars.com - which is in your config.php file of the moodle. ResponsesInList.Text: If you typed this in: certbot --apache -d lms.ecoleinternationalethestars.com -d www.lms.ecoleinternationalethestars.com Then you requested 2 certs - 1 for each of those FQDN's. In CentOS 9, the config for certs is in /etc/httpd/conf file httpd-le-ssl.conf In the above file: SSLCertificateFile - path to file in /etc/letsencrypt/live/[FQDN] SSLCertificateKeyFile - a path to file in /etc/letsencrypt/live/[FQDN] Include /etc/letsencrypt/options-ssl-apache.conf in /etc/letsencrypt/live/ I have only one FQDN directory ... that of the domain I used when setting it up. There is very important README file that says: "This directory contains your keys and certificates. `[cert name]/privkey.pem`  : the private key for your certificate. `[cert name]/fullchain.pem`: the certificate file used in most server software. `[cert name]/chain.pem`    : used for OCSP stapling in Nginx >=1.3.7. `[cert name]/cert.pem`     : will break many server configurations, and should not be used without reading further documentation (see link below). WARNING: DO NOT MOVE OR RENAME THESE FILES! Certbot expects these files to remain in this location in order to function properly! We recommend not moving these files. For more information, see the Certbot User Guide at https://certbot.eff.org/docs/using.html#where-are-my-certificates . Also, if you have the lock icon in browser that can give you more info when viewing certificate. 3 tabs domain, then R3 and ISRG Root X1 on mine The last one when viewed does have a section called Micellaneos and one can download the PEM (cert) as well as the PEM (chain) files. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mobile app login is accessing lib/ajax/service.php and failing with security error
ResponsesInList.Text:
For anyone else who ends up here, we found the problem was related with the configuration in the server. Although I don't know the exact details as this is something specific to their environment, but it doesn't seem to be a problem with the app. At first, I was also puzzled because as Chandra mentioned the following request returned the proper response: 
```text
curl -X POST '
https://mymoodleserver.org/learn/lib/ajax/service.php?info=tool_mobile_get_public_config'
 --data-binary '[{"index":0,"methodname":"tool_mobile_get_public_config","args":{}}]'
```
 But after some tinkering I found out that doing the request with the same headers as the app, it returned a 404: 
```text
curl \
  --request POST \
  --url '
https://mymoodleserver.org/learn/lib/ajax/service.php?info=tool_mobile_get_public_config'
 \
  --header 'Accept-Charset: UTF-8' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 11; sdk_gphone_x86 Build/RSR1.201013.001; wv) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/4.0 Chrome/83.0.4103.106 Mobile Safari/537.36 MoodleMobile 4.2.0 (42000)' \
  --data '[
  {
    "index": 0,
    "methodname": "tool_mobile_get_public_config",
    "args": {}
  }
]'
```
 So, the lesson to learn, always use the same headers to debug . The User-Agent header may change depending on the platform though, but the general idea should be the same.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mobile app login is accessing lib/ajax/service.php and failing with security error
ResponsesInList.Text: Dear Noel, Thank you, thank you! Oh, of course I should have used the *exact* same request in curl, header and all ! Thanks for pointing it out. Now I did try with the headers, and narrowed it down to the "Accept-Charset: UTF-8" header in the mobile app's request as the problem. Without this header, curl works, and with this header, curl fails with 404. It looks like the network security software on my server is suspicious of requests with this header. Since the header has been "deprecated" for a while and modern browsers do not send this value any longer, the security software thinks the request is coming from a rogue script and blocking it. I temporarily disabled this security check on my server, and I am able to login now from the app! woohoo. Knowing what I know now, I was looking around the mobile app's source code and the issue tracker and surprise, surprise, I found an issue has been raised against the mobile app just last week to remove this header !! This one: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-78198 My server uses standard open source ModSec security rules. I'll share more details here for anyone hitting this issue in future. Have a good day, and thanks for your inputs to isolate the issue.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mobile app login is accessing lib/ajax/service.php and failing with security error
ResponsesInList.Text: I have added my analysis here, with details of which ModSecurity rule triggers the problem: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-78198

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mobile app login is accessing lib/ajax/service.php and failing with security error
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for sharing the details, I wasn't aware of that issue. I've opened a new one for the mobile app, the issue you mentioned is only for the LMS and it wouldn't fix the problem in the app. You can keep track of this here: MOBILE-4342 .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mobile app login is accessing lib/ajax/service.php and failing with security error
ResponsesInList.Text: While the issue MOBILE-4342 is resolved in a future release, summarizing the issue and sharing the details of the workaround here. ModSecurity is an open source web application firewall. The default core rule set in ModSec contains a rule that rejects HTTP requests with a 404 (quite harsh in my opinion) when the requests contain the header 'Accept-Charset'. The relevant rule # is 920450, but the header restrictions in the rule are imported via rule # 901165. The workaround is to customize the rule and take out the above header from the list of restricted headers. I have tested this on my server, users are able to use the mobile app as before. 1. You can setup the rule to execute only when it is your specific Moodle URL that is being accessed to minimize impact to other web apps on your server. 2. Preferably, edit a copy of the rule as a new custom rule and enable it, and disable the original rule. Revert to the original and delete the custom when MOBILE-4342 is closed.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Android App Issue with Scorm
ResponsesInList.Text: To play the package the Mobile app must download the zip to the device then unzip it - how big is the SCORM package once unzipped? - if it's 300MB unzipped you will need at least 300MB + 160MB (460MB) free storage on the mobile device (it will delete the zip file, but not until "after" it has successfully unzipped it.) - but 160MB is quite high, you might consider pulling out some of the larger assets (videos etc) and embedding them differently so they are not required inside the zip, but embedded from an external source. ResponsesInList.Title: Data sync between web application & mobile app
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Team, I have few questions in my mind, How will the branded app connects to the database ? what is the frequency data gets synced in both web application & Moodle app? Will mobile app also have local db in place for the data storage? Thanks in advance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Data sync between web application & mobile app
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, the Moodle app communicates with the server using WebServices . So for example when the user opens the "My courses" page, we call the appropriate WebServices to retrieve that info. The app has a cache system (using a local database) to avoid calling the server too often. So for example if a user opens a certain course several times in a short time, the first time the app will perform a request to the server to obtain the latest data but the following requests will use the data that is already stored in the device. This system is the one that allows the app to work in offline. The "valid time" of the information depends of the WebService (whether the data retrieved can change often or not), and it can go from 7 minutes to 18 hours. In general there is no synchronization system to keep this information up to date, it will be updated the next time the user opens the page in online and the data is no longer "valid". When a user tries to create/edit/delete something in offline and the app allows it, we store the data in a local database to be sent when the user is connected. There are several factors that can impact how often we try to send the offline data to the server, the app usually waits 5 - 15 minutes between retries (e.g. if the server is down). So yes, the app has a local db to store the data (it uses sql ite). Cheers, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: GitHub repository branch name changes
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all! We wanted to share with you an important update regarding our development branches on the GitHub repository. Recently, we've changed the name of our development branch from "integration" to "main". As a result of this change, the "main" branch is now the default branch and the "master" branch has been removed from our repository. Moving forward, you can find the stable version of our software in the latest GitHub release tag. We will continue to update and maintain the release tags as new versions are released. In addition, you can notice there are version-named branches. We want to clarify that having branches containing the numbers of the major versions does not mean that we will maintain several versions at the same time. These changes align with the growing trend in the open-source community to move away from using terms with a negative connotation such as "master" or "slave", and towards more inclusive language. We believe that changing the name of the default branch is an important step towards creating a more welcoming and inclusive environment for everyone who contributes to our project. We have already updated our documentation and automated tools to reflect these changes, and we encourage all contributors to do the same. If you have any questions or concerns about these changes, please don't hesitate to reach out. Thank you for your continued support. Kind regards, Pau

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: H5P on Moodle App
ResponsesInList.Text: I worked out a way to use h5p activities on mobile. But it is not secure, so not recommended. 1, create a h5p activity in a course. 2, create a page activity 3, get the embed code from the h5p activity and paste in the page activity. 4, in Home -> Site administration -> Security -> HTTP security -> Allow frame embedding App user should be able to see the h5p activity on mobile now. If you want to record the user activity, you need another plugin, generico filter, I added a  generico filter template like this: <iframe id="embed_h5p_with_user" src="https://yourmoodle.com/mod/hvp/embed.php?id=@@h5p_id@@&user_id=@@USER:ID@@"  width="750" height="1334" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen"></iframe> Copy the h5p activity id, then edit the page activity, use the generico filter template you just created, input the id. also add 4 lines to moodle/mod/hvp/embed.php  before  try{}catch{} if(isset($_GET['user_id'] && $_GET['user_id'])){ $USER = $DB->get_record('user', array('id' => $user_id)); $PAGE->set_context(context_system::instance()); } now the embeded code should work on mobile app.

ResponsesInList.Text: I have added a new php file embed_with_user.php (added some code based on embed.php) to moodle\mod\hvp, the file has been attached. I have also added some check to make sure the request is from moodle mobile app. so change the generico filter template to <iframe id="embed_h5p_with_user" src="https://yourmoodle.com/mod/hvp/embed_with_user.php?id=@@h5p_id@@&user_id=@@USER:ID@@"  width="750" height="1334" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen"></iframe> So the full process is: 1, download embed_with_user.php put it under moodle\mod\hvp 2,in Home -> Site administration -> Security -> HTTP security -> Allow frame embedding 3,install plugin generico filter, 4,add a  generico filter template like this: <iframe id="embed_h5p_with_user" src="https://yourmoodle.com/mod/hvp/embed_with_user.php?id=@@h5p_id@@&user_id=@@USER:ID@@"  width="750" height="1334" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen"></iframe> 5, create a h5p activity in a course. and copy the activity id, set visibility to hidden 6, create a page activity, in page content area, use the generico filter template you just created, input the id.
