ResponsesInList.Title: Is there a way of tracking Moodle Mobile via analytics tool?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone, I've been asked about what percentage of the use of our Moodle instances from mobile devices come from the mobile app. I've done a little research and seen that the usage of the app is logged in the standard log (origin ='ws', in our), but in the log there is not information about the devices used. In our case we use a analytic tool (Google Analytics) which does track the device used, but it groups the activity in "visits", so there is no way to compare that information with the one in the log. So, is there a way of tracking Moodle Mobile via an analytics tool (adding some additional HTML...)?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is there a way of tracking Moodle Mobile via analytics tool?
ResponsesInList.Text: Like other needs in the area of reporting, Moodle lacks ... but doesn't mean the info isn't there if one is willing to dig and do some more. There's more than meets the eye in Moodle. Like browsers, Moodle needs info on devices that connect. mdl_user_devices table holds info: select userid, concat('',model,''), platform,version from `mdl_user_devices The above provides a column listing of userID, the model is linked to a google search for that model of device, and shows platform and version of the Mobile OS as ID'd by the moblie device. You'll have to do the calculation of percentage of usage etc. but at least it's a start. ;) 'spirit of sharing', Ken

ResponsesInList.Title: Er: Re: Is there a way of tracking Moodle Mobile via analytics tool?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Ken and thanks for answering! I knew about user devices table, but if I'm not wrong in that table are only stored the devices that have accessed Moodle via the mobile app (a device that only has connected to Moodle using a browser isn't there); anyway, AFAIK there is no way to join that information with the log so I cannot know how many clics from a user came from that mobile device and how many came from a computer. As a workaround what I've done is this: 1.- Querying the log I can know the percent of clicks that came from the mobile app (origin='ws') by month: SELECT to_char(to_timestamp("timecreated"),'YYYY') as year, to_char(to_timestamp("timecreated"),'MM') as month, count(*) FROM m_logstore_standard_log m WHERE m.origin='ws' GROUP BY to_char(to_timestamp("timecreated"),'YYYY'), to_char(to_timestamp("timecreated"),'MM') ORDER BY to_char(to_timestamp("timecreated"),'YYYY'), to_char(to_timestamp("timecreated"),'MM') ; 2.- I can know from our analytic tool the percent of visits that came from mobile devices Using these percents I can have an approximation of the usage of the mobile app vs. usage of mobile devices. Anyway, in order to have accurate data I think it should be done one of these improvements: Register some info about the device in the Moodle log Make it possible to track the app usage via an analytic tool. Ondo izan. P.S.: As an extra ball, I've done some changes in the query to know how many distinct users connected to Moodle using the app by month: SELECT to_char(to_timestamp("timecreated"),'YYYY') as year, to_char(to_timestamp("timecreated"),'MM') as month, count(distinct userid) as distinct_users FROM mdl_logstore_standard_log m WHERE m.origin='ws' GROUP BY to_char(to_timestamp("timecreated"),'YYYY'), to_char(to_timestamp("timecreated"),'MM') ORDER BY to_char(to_timestamp("timecreated"),'YYYY'), to_char(to_timestamp("timecreated"),'MM') ;

ResponsesInList.Title: Using a html file project to access offline content from the app
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, In order to make our content available offline we have designed a html based project which can be opened in the mobile browser and uses local storage to access the content. Everything worked well except for the indexpage not opening some of the files which are our custom extensions (encrypted files to be opened in another app). These files are linked with the intent property of android chrome and are working fine if you open the index file normally and not from MM2. It also did not allow to install this external app and other apps from the index file which could be helpful for users. And the html pages with pictures did not open as responsive pages and got distorted. Please see the index file to get more clarity. Please suggest ways to create a separate folder in internal or external storage directories to save the files rather than the file being getting saved in Android->data->site..folder. Like Shareit or other apps creating a separate folder in directory. Also kindly help to resolve these issues of opening intent linked files and relative file path in a html file. You can also test this as it is an auto enrolment course and you can login with Google at www.saamarthyaved.com Thanks in advance, Sourabh

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using a html file project to access offline content from the app
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sourabh, I don't understand much what you're trying to achieve, so maybe some of my comments don't make any sense. Can't you include the "offline content asset folder" in the same resource as the index HTML? That way the users wouldn't have to manually paste it. You can use an HTML mini-site, that is, create a new activity of type "File", add ALL the files in there and use the index HTML as the main file. In this case, the app downloads all the files inside the same folder, isolated from the rest of the activities , and opens the main file in an iframe. Regarding the intent problem, I guess it's the data-hasintent and data-contentpath properties, right? I didn't know about them, we'll take a look to see if we can make them work inside the app. Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: change app default language
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi mojtaba, you can see how the current language is determined in here: https://github.com/moodlehq/moodlemobile2/blob/master/www/core/lib/lang.js#L60 The priority order is: Language set using app settings. Device language. Default language. Please notice that if any of the languages above isn't found, fallback language will be used. Fallback language is 'en' by default, you can change it in that same file: https://github.com/moodlehq/moodlemobile2/blob/master/www/core/lib/lang.js#L27 https://github.com/moodlehq/moodlemobile2/blob/master/www/core/lib/lang.js#L161 Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: change app default language
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mojtaba, I think the easiest way to achieve what you want is to just remove the point 2, the device globalization check. That way if the user doesn't have any language manually configured it's going to use the default language (fa).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Not opening SCORM download screen on mobile moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Nitin, the error "Invalid response value detected" means there's something wrong in there. Can you please send us a test account to mobile@moodle.com? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Notifications option don't update info
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sergio, please make sure you are connected and your Moodle is available when accessing the Notifications option. Please notice that the notifications shown in here are the same that are shown in the following option of Moodle web: Messages > Recent Notifications Some push notifications (like messages received) aren't reflected in the notifications table. If after verifying all this you still think this isn't working, you'll have to check Network requests in the Chrome/Safari inspector and check if the WS call is failing or not (you can use a Pull to refresh to force a WS call). Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Plans for supporting moodle additional (contributed) plugins in the Mobile app
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, we are working in a new feature for Moodle 3.1: "Supporting Moodle plugins in the mobile app", basically this means that we want to allow Moodle plugins developers to make their plugins compatible with the Mobile app. With this new feature, plugins like the progress bar, certificate, questionnaire and any question type or quiz access rules would be able to be displayed in the Mobile app as a new option in the menu or in another place (depending of the type of plugin). We've been working in a spec and a proof of concept, here you have the relevant links: The first presentation we did about this new feature in the last developer meeting (where some terms are explained) The first draft and feedback from other Moodle developers (please, read only the comments because the document was moved to the dev wiki - see following link-) The initial spec in the dev wiki The relevant Moodle issues: MDL-49279 and MOBILE-925 ﻿ We'd like to hear your feedback in this discussion. Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Hittesh, yes, that means that developers will have to write an AngularJs module for the app, in some cases it would be just implementing a basic interface but in another cases (complex modules) it will require more work. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MMW2.1 - Activity Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Tim, did you see the Page using the Mobile app or Moodle web? When you see a Page using the Mobile app, the app calls the WS mod_page_view_page . This WS is only available in the master version of Moodle (not released) and also in local_mobile (Moodle Mobile Additional Features). If your Moodle version is lower and you don't have the local_mobile plugin installed then viewing the page in the app won't mark it as viewed. If you fulfill any of the previous conditions, then seeing the Page in the app should update the completion status both in Moodle and in the app as long as you're online. If it's not immediately updated in the app you can try to perform a pull to refresh in the page where you see the module completion. You can always check the status in Moodle web to be sure if the app has updated it or not. I hope this helps you, Dani

I have Completion Tracking enabled in my courses and I'm sure that previously when a student clicked on an activity, viewed it, then returned to the course page there was a tick next to the activity to indicate it had been completed. That doesn't seem to be working anymore. The boxes now need to be manually ticked. Except for the 'pages' activities , they seem to tick automatically. I noticed the boxes for those ticks are dotted lines rather than solid. Is anyone aware of any reason why completion tracking would not be working? I have the option of looking into the completion tracking settings but it would mean wiping the data and starting again apparently, according to the message that Moodle gives me. Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MMW2.1 - Activity Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jacques, if activity completion is enabled in your course, if you edit an activity you'll see an "Activity Completion" section. In there you'll see a "Completion tracking option" that can be configured to the following: Do not indicate activity completion -> Disabled. Students can manually mark the activity as completed -> The student needs to manually click the checkbox to mark it as completed. Show activity as completed when conditions are met -> The checkbox will be automatically marked when certain conditions are done. I guess your activities aren't configured as you want to. As you say, modifying this value will erase all the completion data of that activity so all students will see it as not completed. Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MMW2.1 - Activity Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dani, Thanks for your help. With "Show activity as completed when conditions are met" can I set it up so the person just has to click on/open the activity and then when they navigate back the activity is marked as completed? Also modifying the value will wipe the data so students won't see what has been completed, but will the Admin still be able to see what has been completed? Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MMW2.1 - Activity Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jacques, yes, you can configure the activities to complete when the user views them. Regarding your other question, all the completion data in that activity will be deleted, so there will be no trace left for any user. You have more information about activity completion in here: https://docs.moodle.org/31/en/Activity_completion Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MMW2.1 - Activity Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Dani, Ok I think what I'll do is wipe the data for each activity but I'll keep a physical record of which users have completed which activities. As an Admin can I then go into the completion tracking report and referring to the physical record go through and manually tick off the activities that the users have completed? Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MMW2.1 - Activity Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jacques, I think you can't change a student's completion from the completion tracking report. You'll have to do a "Login in as" for each student and mark the activities as completed. The "Login in as" is in: In Moodle 3.0 or higher, go to course participants, go to the profile of the user and then you'll find the feature. In previous versions, in the navigation block. The other option is to manually modify the Moodle database , but I don't think that'll be easy. Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MMW2.1 - Activity Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Dani!

I just read to enable Activity Completion I need to have Course Administration and Student Progress. To enable Student Progress I apparently have to go into settings under Course Administration? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MMW2.1 - Activity Completion
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jacques, you shouldn't need any external plugin. You need to (taken from the docs): In Administration > Site administration > Advanced features check the " Enable completion tracking " box. In Administration > Course administration > Edit settings set " Enable completion tracking " to Yes . Then in each activity you should see the activity completion section. Each activity needs to be configured itself. Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MoodleMobile access via browser only for SSO?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Juan, We were able to finally resolve the issue. It appears that the app is connecting over https by default for generating the token and then the connection changes over to http. This was resetting the referrer header and the app was not getting launched through the browser after login. We fixed it by forbidding https connections for token.php via an apache directive. 
```text
This is fixed by forbidding https connections on the path {code}/login/token.php{code}. The following apache directive was included to achieve the effect:
{code}
<Location /login/token.php>
        RewriteEngine On
        RewriteCond %{HTTPS} on
        RewriteRule (.*) 
http://%
{HTTP_HOST}%{REQUEST_URI} [F]
</Location>
{code}
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Lost Connection.  Your Token is now Invalid.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jason, the first error is because the token has expired. The app uses a token to communicate to the server without having to enter the user credentials, and for security reasons these tokens are invalidated after a certain time (usually 3 months). The only way to fix it is to input the credentials again. In MoodleMobile2 (Android and iPhone), when this error happens the user will be prompted with a screen to enter his password again. Unfortunately this version isn't compatible with Windows, so in Windows the user will have to leave the site and add it again (there's no need to delete it, you should be able to add a site that's already stored and it should update the token). ResponsesInList.Title: Ang: Re: Play Video Offline in moodle mobile App
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Juan, I thought it easier to catch you here as well (so others can also follow the development). We are really interested in using the option for offline video, but we also really like the fact that video can be embedded directly into the text field in a topic, so you don't have to click more than necessary to get to it. First of all, it seems that embedded videos (even when uploaded to moodle as well) are not downloadable for offline use, correct? Taking this into consideration we then tried something else: inserting a video as an activity (so it can be downloaded) and then linking to it within moodle in the text field. However, this makes the app open the phone's web browser instead of staying in the app. This seems to be a problem all through the app. If I write a text strip identical to the name of an activity it automatically makes it into a link in the text field, which is actually fine. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Ang: Re: Play Video Offline in moodle mobile App
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Christoffer, embedded videos are only downloaded by the app if they are uploaded to Moodle and linked using pluginfile.php (Moodle script to serve files). These videos will be downloaded in the following cases: When the user loads a page containing a video (not playing it): If the user is using a limited connection (not wifi) and the video size is less than 2MB, it will be downloaded. If the user is using a wifi connection and the video size is less than 20MB , it will be downloaded. From Moodle Mobile 3.1 (released this week), when the user plays a video or audio: If the user is using a wifi connection the file will be downloaded. Please notice that these downloads will start in background and the embedded video will load the online one. The downloaded files will be loaded the next time the user loads the view. Regarding linking activities in the content, it's something we started supporting in Moodle Mobile 2.9. If you add a link to mod/resource/view.php?id=XX (activity auto-linking does that), the app should capture it and redirect the user to that resource inside the app. However, in order to make it work you need to have Moodle 3.0+ or the Moodle Mobile Additional Features installed. There's a workaround to make it work in older versions without the plugin: you need to add the courseid in the param. That is: mod/resource/view.php?id=XX &courseid=YY . With this you should be able to make it work. If this isn't working for you we'd like to test it so we can check what's going on (same user as before?). Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Logout for Multiple Users Sharing Same Device

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Custom login Page

If you've set your development environment following this guide then you should place your CSS code in a SCSS file and then run gulp to build the final CSS. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle mobile works OK in two sites, but KO on the remaining
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi again, the first site fails because of the redirect. When you enter your credentials, the app performs a request to MOODLEURL/login/token.php, where MOODLEURL is the URL you entered in the first screen. Since you have that redirect, the request ends up being sent to: http://moodle.uco.es/exa/course/index.php?categoryid=2/login/token.php That URL isn't valid, so the login fails. Regarding the other URL, I tested adding an invalid username and your server is returning some debugging data that it shouldn't. The request to login/token.php should return only a JSON string, but in your site it's returning some text outside of the JSON and that's causing the app to fail because it expects a JSON. I'll send you a private message with more details. Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle mobile works OK in two sites, but KO on the remaining

In our case, it was associated with the external database authentication. In order to avoid the problem, the choice "ADPdb debug" must be set to "No" in the External Database Authentication plugin. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: In Moodle Book image is not shown
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle parses all CSS files. When theme designer mode is off, Moodle combines them into a handful of large CSS files that get cached and served. At the same time Moodle also looks at the CSS and replaces special syntax rules. [[pix:theme|path/to/image/imagename]] The above pattern is looked for by Moodle and gets replaced with the correct image  when found. You should note the following things about this pattern when using your own images within CSS: The bits in black don't change The bit in blue is the path to your image within the pix directory. It shouldn't start with a / but should end with one. The bit in green is the filename (no need to include the file extension) To use background.png as the background for our pages, add the following line of CSS to the themes core.css. body {background-image:url([[pix:theme|gradient]]);} Before we look at how to use your own images within your themes layout files we should first look at how this changes if the image is in a sub directory. Lets assume gradient.png is located here: pix/myimages/gradients/gradient.png The CSS would need to be as follows: body {background-image:url([[pix:theme|myimages/gradients/gradient]]);} If you want to refer to an image belonging to a plugin, you can do it like this: body {background-image:url([[pix:quiz|icon]]);} body {background-image:url([[pix:qtype_ddmarker|grid]]);} That refers to mod/quiz/pix/icon.png/gif and question/type/ddmarker/pix/grid.png/gif respectively (or whatever icons you have put in your theme to override these).

ResponsesInList.Title: Changes in Moodle Mobile release process
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, we've made some changes in the Moodle Mobile release process: Frequency: Until now we were releasing a new version per month (some months we released two versions). In order to make the release process more sustainable and to improve our Q&A process, we will be releasing new versions every two months starting soon (probably when Moodle 3.1 is released). The plan will be to release new versions at the same time (same week) that new major or minor Moodle versions are released. Versioning: Once we start releasing along Moodle, we’ll align Moodle version numbers with the Moodle Mobile ones. Once Moodle 3.1 is released, we’ll release Moodle Mobile 3.1.0. Every time minor Moodle versions are released we’ll increase the last digit so, for example, when Moodle 3.1.1 is out, we’ll release Moodle Mobile 3.1.1. The second digit will be increased when Moodle major versions are released. Hopefully, this will avoid confusions with the version numbering between Moodle and Moodle Mobile. Emergency releases: In some cases, we’ll need to release a new version at a different time than a Moodle one. When this happens, we will increase the last digit too.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Playing mp3 audio files in mobile App (v. 2.8)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Oliver, the problem is that right now the app looks for the file extension in the URL of the files, so if a URL doesn't contain the file extension then it's going to be downloaded without extension. It was implemented like this to make it faster, simpler and decrease the network usage. We have an open issue to improve it: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MOBILE-1455 New Moodle versions should automatically add the extension of a file when you upload it, or at least it does it for me. In your case, the URL to the file doesn't contain the extension. Android is able to open the file without having the extension (at least in my phone), but iOS can't. As a temporary solution, you could modify the file to add the extension to the file name, that way it should work in the Moodle Mobile app. Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Audio in Moodle Mobile
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, well, the main problem is that Phonegap (that is the library/framework we use for cross-compiling and also for using Mobile functionallities from an HTML5 app) only support these formats for capturing audio/video: `video/3gpp (mp4 also) Android` `video/quicktime iOs` `image/jpeg` `audio/amr Android` `audio/wav iOs` So we will need a plugin/external library for converting audio to ogg or mp3. Since we need to compile for both Android and iOs using a online service called PhonegapBuild, we need to use only plugins supported by that service. Unfortunately there are no plugins for converting formats currently supported. Currently we are more focusing in polish the Push notification functionality and adding support for Android GCM (Notifications) Regards

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem viewing mod_resources objects in custom app.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi again, to open mod_resource PDF files we use the function $mmUtil.openFile . In Android we use the WebIntent plugin ( net.tunts.webintent ) to open the file in other apps using the dialog you mentioned in the first post. If for some reason the variable window.plugins doesn't exist, we open the link using: window.open(path, '_blank'); This window.open is captured by InAppBrowser, resulting in the view in your screenshot. So my guess is that window.plugins variable doesn't exist in your build, maybe the plugin net.tunts.webintent wasn't installed correctly. If you want to debug what's going on I suggest you to look at the $mmUtil.openFile function. Kind regards, Dani

Can you help me understand what scenarios could cause a response... {"error":0,"code":"2"} Using / local/mobile/check.php?service=local_mobile I'm trying to understand the response errors for the Moodle Mobile Additional Features plugin http://examplenoodlesite.com/ local/mobile/check.php?service=local_mobile When configured properly: {"error":0,"code":"1"} When plugin installed but not-enabled: {"error":1,"code":3} Do you know what scenarios cause the following response? {"error":0,"code":"2"} Thanks, Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scenarios for response codes on Moodle Mobile Additional Features plugin check.php
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Anthony, there is no {"error":0,"code":"2"} scenario, we used {"error":0,"code":"1"} for saying that everything was ok so I can use further OK codes error:0, code: 2 etc.. in the future for describing specific configurations or settings that may be required in the bootstrap phase. So basically, right now, error:0 means everything ok, but in the future the code may change to reflect some specific settings/configurations Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scenarios for response codes on Moodle Mobile Additional Features plugin check.php
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Juan, Thanks for your reply. Our client site was returning that unusual response code, so I needed to do some more digging. I found out what setting returns. {"error":0,"code":"2"} I've documented it incase others find it helpful. Change Site Administration > Plugins > Local Plugins > Moodle Mobile additional features : Switch Type of Login to "Via a browser window (for SSO plugins)" Test: http://yourmoodlesite.com/local/mobile/check.php?service=moodle_mobile This will return: ``` {"error":0,"code":"2"} ``` If select Type of Login: "Via the app" Test: http://yourmoodlesite.com/local/mobile/check.php?service=moodle_mobile returns... ``` {"error":0,"code":"1"} ``` The back-porting of the web services api in the MM additional features plugin is very useful. Your team's work on this is much appreciated. Thanks, Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scenarios for response codes on Moodle Mobile Additional Features plugin check.php
ResponsesInList.Text: Oh, sorry, you are right! I missed that scenario, it was a long time ago when I did it Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Scenarios for response codes on Moodle Mobile Additional Features plugin check.php

Hi again, if  you're testing in a browser you should start it without security to allow requests without CORS. We recommend using Chrome or Chromium, here's how to start it. Chrome in Windows: 
```text
"Path to chrome\chrome.exe" --allow-file-access-from-files --disable-web-security
```
 Chrome in Mac: 
```text
open -a "Google Chrome" --args --allow-file-access-from-files --disable-web-security
```
 Chromium in Mac: 
```text
open -a /Applications/Chromium.app --args --allow-file-access-from-files --disable-web-security
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem with Moodle 2.6.4 + Moodle mobile 2.7
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Cyrus, your screenshot confirms me that the problem is due to the feature to download sections. In 2.7 we introduced this feature that allows users to download a whole section by clicking the download button next to it. The problem is that we need to check the status of all the resources of a section to be able to determine which button to show, so if a section has a lot of resources  this can be slow. We have a memory "cache" to speed up this process, but it's emptied when the app is closed. The only solution we found is to allow disabling this feature. We'll probably introduce a new setting in "App Settings" so any user can disable this feature. If they disable it then the contents should be loaded faster (like in 2.6), but they won't be able to download a whole section at once. Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to pre-populate and hide site URL entry page?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sourabh, I tested it and your Moodle opened MoodleMobile official app after authenticating. If you haven't done it already, you should change the URL scheme your app uses ( see the plugin documentation ). You should also change the URL scheme used by your local mobile in Moodle. Inside local_mobile plugin there's a file named launch.php with this line: $location = "Location: moodlemobile://token=$apptoken"; If you change "moodlemobile" with your URL scheme it should open your app, but then it won't work for the official Moodle Mobile app. If you want it to work both for your custom app and for MoodleMobile then you'll have to create a new script. You can just duplicate launch.php ( with another name) and use your custom URL scheme in that new script. You should call this new script in your custom app, that is done in www/core/components/login/services/helper.js: var loginurl = siteurl + "/local/mobile/launch.php?service=" + mmCoreConfigConstants.wsextservice; You should replace "local/mobile/launch.php" with the location of your new script. I hope this helps! Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to pre-populate and hide site URL entry page?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Yezi, seems Juan's changes to the PPT weren't saved, we just fixed it so it no longer talks about changing main.js. About your problem, have you run gulp after adding that to the config file? In 2.7 we changed the way we read the config values to make it faster and simpler to retrieve them. Now the gulp process converts the JSON file into an Angular constant, and we read the values from that constant. This means that you need to run gulp everytime you change the config.json file. If you don't have the development environment set, you can manually apply it to the build file (although it's not recommended since it can give you problems during rebase). If you go to the end of build/mm.bundle.js you'll see something like this: .constant('mmCoreConfigConstants', { "app_id" : "com.moodle.moodlemobile", "versioncode" : "2007", "versionname" : "2.6", "cache_expiration_time" : 300000, "default_lang" : "en", "languages": {...}, "wsservice" : "moodle_mobile_app", "wsextservice" : "local_mobile", "demo_sites": {...}, "gcmpn": "694767596569" } You can add the siteurl in there too. I hope this helps fixing the problem! Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A required parameter (username) was missing.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Alexander, I've taken a look and the problem is caused by a redirect. The app checks if https is available in your site, and it is so the login request is done to https (please notice that the URL written when you type username and password has https in it) . Your server is configured to redirect https requests to http, but the app cannot follow these kind of redirects so the login fails. The only solution I can give you right now is to disable https in your site so the check detects it's not enabled and it performs the login using http. I don't know if you can disable it only in a certain script, if it's possible then disabling https in prestigemedical.org/online/login/token.php should be enough. I'm sorry but right now that's the only solution. Kind regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sourabh, Our solution ended up being a little convoluted and much of this response is supposition rather than known fact. The problem was with shibboleth and the time being taken from shibboleth authentication through to returning to the mobile app. Although moodle was generating the token correctly, the connection seemed to timeout rather than return the token. What we have ended up doing is creating a second ldap connection and authenticating staff through one ldap directory and students through a different one. This has allowed us to remove shibboleth completely from Moodle which I suspect might not be an option for you. This has fixed the problem with the mobile app and removed the need to direct to the web browser and has also fixed a number of other issues we were having with the time taken for an authentication response. e.g. Moodle flagging up that you were already logged in despite it being your first attempt. I'm more than happy to share our code for a second ldap connection if this is of use to you. Thanks, Edd

```text
$resp
 = 
$curl
->
post
(
$serverurl
, 
$params
);
```

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I'm developing Mobile app add on that communicates with custom local plugin in Moodle 2.6. One scenario of use I need to cover is to provide some personalized interventions based on certain user action. For example, when user visit some page, several sub-plugins in the Moodle web application will be triggered, and some of them might provide certain intervention such as warning, recommendation, etc. The problem is in that these sub-plugins are to be developed based on machine learning algorithms, and sometimes it might take some time for processing, so user might have a warning produced immediately, and recommendation might be produced 30 seconds later, or he might have no intervention. I thought that pushing this interventions from Moodle web application to Mobile device might  be more efficient then having a poll that will check in frequent intervals if there is some intervention for user to be displayed. At least, there will be no delays in providing feedback. However, I've never used push notifications and I'm not sure if it could be used in this way, and if it is the best solution for my scenario. The other thing is that I don't want users to have to enable push notifications in order to make it work. It should always work. I would appreciate any advice on this issue. Thanks, Zoran

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Customizing push notifications for data exchange
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I'd recommend you to do that via message outputs https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Messaging_2.0 that they are connected with Mobile notifications right now. The only problem I see is that you want everything automatically enabled, in that case, I'd suggest you to create a new external function (Web Service) to be called by the Mobile application (for example, listening the SiteUpdate event https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Moodle_Mobile#Events ) to force the user messaging profile settings for the Mobile notifications output system to be on Another potential issue is that you will need your own Airnotifier server if you want the app to work on iOs too. Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Customizing push notifications for data exchange
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Zoran, to clarify: If you have developed an app for Android only, you can use the public Airnotifier installation after registering your site (you can also use a custom installation too). If you have developed an app for both Android and iOs (or only iOs) you will need to use a custom Airnotifier installation. ==================================================================== The technical reason is that for iOs you need to create certificates linked to your custom app , but for Android you use a generic API key (so you can use the same API key in different apps) Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Single app mode on iPad
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi lisa, as far as I know apps don't have to do anything specific to use iOS Guided Access (aka Single app mode). You can use that to lock users into the app you want. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Mobile Usage Reports and Activity Logs
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, Usage reports: See this thread https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=321074 Synchronization and offline: Yes, you can use the app offline but once is back online  the activity is not synchronized (mainly because Moodle does not support asynchronous activity so we cannot add log entries of passed dates) Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Mobile Usage Reports and Activity Logs
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello again, no, currently there is no way for collecting those statistics, in any case, only  the "read data operations" are the ones not be synchronized, for example, reading a page or opening a PDF in the app. The rest of operations - read or update - (like posting in a forum, etc...) will be always logged, for example, we are working in a feature for posting offline, in that case, the action will be logged once the post is synchronized. Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Analytics / reports on app usage
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Im trying to measure user use of the app for moodle. I've google analytics running on the site and I can see that about 20-25% of the traffic in a given week is mobile based. However there is no specific data on App or App ID's as far as I can tell. So I cannot differentiate between a user accessing via the app and one using a mobile browser. Any suggestions on how this might be tracked/measured? Thanks Daniel

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Analytics / reports on app usage
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Daniel, you have two ways for tracking mobile app access: 1. Via the Moodle log. All the accesses using the app are marked with 'ws' in the origin field 2. The app uses Web Services to communicate with Moodle, all the requests done uses always the same endpoint (/webservice/rest/ server .php) and /login/token.php (the first time the user access). So you may filter your logs or analytic tol to see requests for those scripts. Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Analytics / reports on app usage
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Juan That's exactly what I needed. Useful to be able to gauge the use of the mobile app Many thanks for taking the time to reply to this! Daniel

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Analytics / reports on app usage
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey Juan, I need a little more help with this.  I'm using Google Analytics and I don't see any requests in GA for /webservice/rest/server.php or /login/token.php anywhere in GA.  Does the GA code in the Additional HTML settings for the site get applied to the webservice or is this something that I'd have to go in and insert manually? Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Analytics / reports on app usage
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Joshua, I'm afraid you are not going to be able to insert the GA code in the webservice scripts (server.php or login/token.php) because the response format is JSON (not HTML so it's not interpreted by the browser). If you want to measure the app usage you will have to use an external tool for analyzing the server logs (the Apache access_log for example) or, as I said in my original post, analyze the Moodle log filtering entries with origin 'ws'. Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Analytics / reports on app usage
ResponsesInList.Text: Makes sense... I will look at the logs to get a sense of what's going on. With that said, if there is anyway in the future to be able to get this info into GA that would be amazingly helpful.  When I saw this post, I suddenly realized how undercounted all our mobile traffic is in GA...

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Adding third party directive problem
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Zoran, I've never used ng-walkthrough so I can't be of much use to you, but maybe I can give you some advice to debug the problem. Sometimes our $log decorator gets in the middle of error reports, making it unable to know where is the error happening. In those cases I just turn it off replacing this line in core/main.js: $provide.decorator('$log', ['$delegate', $mmLogProvider.logDecorator]); and putting these lines instead: $provide.decorator('$log', ['$delegate', function($log) { $log.getInstance = function(){ return $log; }; return $log; }]); Sometimes you'll have to refresh several times or restart ionic serve to make it work. You'll know it works because the log entries won't have a timestamp anymore. E.g. instead of seeing: "10/13/2015 6:10:46 PM $mmInitDelegate: Executing init process 'mmLogin'" You'll just see: " Executing init process 'mmLogin'" Once you've turned the decorator off, please try to reproduce the error again. This time the error report might be more useful to you. I hope this helps you figure out the problem! Dani

ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for the credentials, this isn't an iOS9 issue, it fails in Android too. I've opened an issue about this: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MOBILE-1237 The problem is that a server call takes too long to respond. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Mobile gives error
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually, it worked before because the app didn't send any data when checking if the site exists. Let me explain myself. When a user types a URL in the app, it sends a request to check if the site exists. In previous versions of MoodleMobile we didn't pass any param to this call, so the script immediately rejected the request. In MOBILE-1144 we decided to send some fake data to this script to be able to use CORS. So now this script checks if the username exists, and that's slower. You can manually emulate this call: <YOURMOODLEURL>/login/token.php?username=a&password=b&service=c You'll notice that if you remove the params then the script immediately rejects the request. Regards, Dani

We will take another look in any case Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Few doubts in the Moodle Mobile 2 customization presentation
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Charles, we use 2 ways of building apps: Ionic CLI (development) and PhoneGap Build (release). Each way have its own configuration and directory structure. The code in 'moodlemobile2' repository is for Ionic CLI, so if you want to build using PhoneGap we recommend creating a new repository or using the moodlemobile-phonegapbuild official repository. If you look at the code in moodlemobile2 repo you'll that there are several folders and files in the root folder: hooks, resources, scss, www, etc. PhoneGap Build only needs what's inside www , the rest of files are for Ionic CLI, so you need to copy what's inside of moodlemobile2/www into the root folder of your new repository (see moodlemobile-phonegapbuild repo). PhoneGap Build also needs a some extra configuration to work, that's why the slides tell you to create a config.xml file, copy the icon and splash, and so. moodlemobile2's config.xml is only for building with Ionic CLI, not with PhoneGap Build, so you don't need to copy that file (use this one as an example to build your own). About page 20, yes it's similar to the presets URL but there's a difference: in MM1 the user could still change the URL, but in here he won't be able to. If you use those steps, then the user will only be able to use your URL. Regards, Dani

You could create a directive that checks if the library is loaded and, if it isn't, performs the code linked above. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Mobile redirect to login page
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David, I can't seem to understand exactly what you're trying to accomplish. As far as I understand, you have an URL resource in your Moodle. As an example, let's say that this activity points to www.google.com . If you use MM app to navigate to that resource and open it, a system browser will be opened with www.google.com . I guess you also added an image with an URL of the kind: " http://mymoodle.net/mod/url/view.php?id=4 ". If you click that image in the app you see the Moodle login form and, after authenticating, you end up in the Moodle URL page where there's a link to www.google.com . What do you want to achieve? Do you want that clicking the image opens www.google.com directly? Or do you want that opening the URL resource sends you to the Moodle URL page like the image do? If you want that opening the Moodle URL resource in the app (open directly www.google.com ) is recorded in the Moodle logs and the activity completion, then you should install the Moodle Mobile Additional Features plugin. If you have that plugin installed, then opening that URL using the app should have the same behavior as opening in Moodle web: a log entry will be added and the URL should be marked as completed if it's configured as " Student must view this activity to complete it ". Regards, Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: URGENT: Potential major blocker - folder activity error message on Moodle 2.8.7
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Yezi, Moodle Mobile project has 2 kind of files: development files and release (auto-built) files. When we develop the app we work using the development files, where each controller/service/directive/whatever has its own file. These files are NOT included in the index.html, they aren't used by the app. When we want these changes to take effect, we "build" the release files (under build/ folder) so the changes made in the development files are reflected in the app. Initially we included these build files in the moodlemobile2 repository, but that caused some integration problems so we finally removed them. In the moodlemobile-phonegapbuild repository these build files are included, so there's no need to manually build them. That means that if you want this change to take effect in the app you have to apply it to the build JS file. In here: https://github.com/moodlehq/moodlemobile-phonegapbuild/blob/master/build/mm.bundle.js#L4802 I hope I made sense Dani

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MM2 - Audio Files not playing
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tim, I had a look at this issue too, it seems that this is coming from network security feature most likely set up by your system administrator. When I accessed your site, I could not listen to the audio clips either. The requests to those files were forbidden with the following message: HTTP/1.1 407 Proxy Authentication Required I am guessing that the request is allowed providing that my proxy details have been set as you'd expect them, which is not something the app has control over. Another thing I noticed is that the URL to your files are pointing to a draft area "draftfile.php". That does not seem right, draft files are temporary and should not be used to serve content. Technically you might be able to access them if you were the user uploading them, but drafts are usually deleted with 4 days. The URL pointing to your resource should contain "pluginfile.php" in order to work both in a browser, and in the app. That problem can often arise when copying content from one place to another. I hope this helps. Cheers, Fred

ResponsesInList.Title: SSL/Mobile App Question
ResponsesInList.Text:
Greetings! Short version of my question: Does the Moodle mobile app require a unique IP address for
each subdomain on a Wildcard SSL certificate? (please realize that I am sort of parroting some of this back from what I've read!) The follow-up question is - Will the app work at all if the main site uses a wildcard certificate? We recently upgraded from 2.8.5 to 2.9.1, and shortly thereafter applied an SSL certificate, giving us an https URL . (By "we" and "us", I mean "not me, but real technicians") I can't connect to the upgraded site with the new mobile app. the message is fairly standard: Error Cannot connect: Verify that you have typed correctly the URL and that your site uses Moodle 2.4 or later. In fact, we have another 2.9.1 site without a certificate that the app connects to just fine. I know that the documentation states: If your site uses a SSL certificate it must be a trusted certificate.
For security reasons the app doesn't work with self-signed
certificates. ( https://docs.moodle.org/29/en/Moodle_Mobile#Moodle_sites_must_be_enabled_for_the_app_to_access_them ) But, as far as I can tell, our certificate is not self-signed (the issuer and subject are different - those would be the same in a self-signed certificate, I understand). When I view the certificate details, the subject field value shows: CN = *.mcpss.com OU = Domain Control Validated I also found the following on GoDaddy's web site: Wildcard certificates secure websites just like regular SSL
certificates, and requests are processed using the same validation
methods. However, some Web servers might require a unique IP address for
each subdomain on the Wildcard certificate. Thanks for any help or direction. I'll be glad to supply more information. David Mobile (coincidentally), Alabama

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle Mobile additional features web service - enabled or not?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi. We're currently in the process of building a brand new Moodle 2.8 environment and I noticed that after installing the latest version of Moodle Moodle additional features plugin its associated web service is not enabled by default: Is this normal? Looking at the service's settings page, it's definitely not enabled: Sorry - just a a bit confused here and would appreciate some clarification. Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Mobile additional features web service - enabled or not?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi, it's not enabled by default since in order to make it work you need to do some additional steps, described here: https://docs.moodle.org/29/en/Moodle_Mobile_additional_features 1. Unpack the zip file into the local/ directory. A new directory will be created called local/mobile. 2. Go to Site administration > Notifications to complete the plugin installation. 3. Go to Site administration > Plugins > Web services >
Mobile, enable "Enable web services for mobile devices" (Remember to
save the changes) 4. Go to Site administration > Plugins > Web services >
External services, edit "Moodle Mobile additional features" and check
the "Enabled" field, then save changes. 5. Go to Site administration > Users >Permissions Define
roles, edit the Authenticated user role and allow the capability
moodle/webservice:createtoken.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Mobile additional features web service - enabled or not?
ResponsesInList.Text: I think part of what the OP was asking was, why does it not enable the mobile web services as part of the install. My guess is that it plugin installer won't change other settings outside of the module its installing?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Mobile additional features web service - enabled or not?

ResponsesInList.Title: MM2 - How to enable addon for individual courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I'm implementing addon for Moodle Mobile 2 and I registered it using $mmCoursesDelegate.registerPlugin, so it's available from the list of the courses. It works fine, but I need to enable/disable it for the individual courses. If teacher did not activate my plugin on the regular Moodle web application for his course, it should not be available for that course in Mobile application too. I implemented external service that receives courseid and returns information if this plugin should be enabled or not for that course. However, I'm not sure how to implement this on the front end. Thanks, Zoran

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MM2 - How to enable addon for individual courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Zoran, You should be able to selectively disable a plugin by defining the method 'isEnabledForCourse()'. See https://github.com/moodlehq/moodlemobile2/blob/master/www/core/components/courses/services/delegate.js#L35 Cheers, Fred

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MM2 - How to enable addon for individual courses
Re: MM2 - How to enable addon for individual courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Zoran, as you say, the function passed to $mmCoursesDelegate.registerPlugin is not the place to check that, in there you only need to check if the plugin is available for the current site. This function is executed when a user logs in a site or the site data is updated. I see you have implemented the isEnabledForCourse function inside $mmaMorph, as the delegate doc says. This function is going to be called for each course, and the courseId is passed as a parameter: https://github.com/moodlehq/moodlemobile2/blob/master/www/core/components/courses/services/delegate.js#L80 So you don't need to manually call that function, it will be automatically called. Hope this helps! Dani

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Thanks for explanation. It seems that support for this has been implemented recently, and I was using moodlemobile2 code which was 3-4 weeks old which didn't have that trigger. Once I updated to the recent code everything started to work fine. Thanks, Zoran

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A question about offline and synchronisation function
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, this is going to change for Moodle Mobile 2. Currently, we do not download the course files in the background, the user has to download or access the content first. This is because course contents can be huge and the storage capacity in a mobile device is limited. Synchronization is currently done mainly for notifications, in Moodle Mobile 2 we are working in a synchronization process (still not implemented) but all the screens will have pull down to refresh to update your contents. Also, synchronization usually happens when you are accesing the course contents view and you are online. Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Cadwell, sorry for my late response. Short answer: Yes, the app forces you to a second login, is a known problem and is in the app roadmap to fix that as soon as possible. ResponsesInList.Title: Problem with Moodle mobile app
ResponsesInList.Text: We have a Moodle 2.9 (Build: 20150511) server at http://moodle2.rncb.ac.uk . This is running on IIS and MySQL with SSL enforced for logging in, and NTLM SSO enabled for the local network. Users are authenticated via LDAP . It works well for browser users. When we try to connect the Moodle mobile app, it gets as far as authenticating the user (and fails if the user isn't valid) but then displays the following error message "Cannot connect:  Verify that you have typed correctly the URL and that your site uses Moodle 2.4 or later." The log for the user concerned seems to show that tokens are working OK, but offers no further insight that i can see: 20 May, 08:59 The web service function 'core_webservice_get_site_info' has been called. 20 May, 08:59 The user with id '12' has been sent the web service token with id '2'. I have read other forums posts about debug logging (not switched on) and SSL problems (our certificate is good, I think), but cannot fathom out why it won't go any further. Is anyone able to offer a suggestion? I am not an experience Moodle admin! Thanks, Nick Brown.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem with Moodle mobile app
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Nick, can I have a test user account to see what is happening in my development environment? If it's possible, you can send me the credentials via private messaging. Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Text: I have done so, thanks very much for your help.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem with Moodle mobile app
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Nick, it's interesting to see that requests using HTTPS works with the mobile app but using HTTP doesn't work. Sample request that works: Request URL: https://moodle2.rncb.ac.uk/webservice/rest/server.php?moodlewsrestformat=json Request Method: POST Status Code: 200 OK and this one doesn't work: Request URL: http://moodle2.rncb.ac.uk/webservice/rest/server.php?moodlewsrestformat=json Request Method: POST Status Code: 401 Unauthorized Request Headers view source The main difference is that the app uses HTTPS for requesting the token and do a first request for retrieve the site settings, in that moment, your Moodle site says that he uses http:// so the app switch to use http:// and then when the app tries to do something, a web server authentication form is displayed (it request username and password). In order to solve this, I see to options: - Use HTTPS for the whole site, not only for authentication - Use the local_mobile plugin, see: https://docs.moodle.org/28/en/Moodle_Mobile_additional_features this will force your uses to authenticate in the Moodle site for retrieving a token Hope it helps, Juan

So I recommended that we try out the Moodle App. This was largely unsuccessful since quite often the app dropped the user back to the browser to carry out particular interactions eg: uploading a video created on the phone could not uploaded without going to a thr bowser, logging into the website (rather than the app) and then uploading in the browser. Also, the sudden change in theme from the app to the website was misleading and confusing. Perhaps a mobile theme is needed which matches the app interface... Hope the feedback is helpful. Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Android App and Uploading etc
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Andrew, thanks a lot for your feedback, we really appreciate it. We are aware of this problem. The main problem with passing user credentials onto the browser (that we usually call SSO - Single Sign On) is that Moodle doesn't support a SSO mechanism. Any new feature in the Mobile app usually requires changes or new development in Moodle (like new web services, new settings, etc...) in this case Moodle is willing to change the SSO mechanism from Mnet to SAML, once is supported in Moodle we will add support to it in the app. We are also working in a new version of the app, that will come with User Interface and improvements so the user experience will be improved and the mobile app will match the Moodle interface, see http://prototype.moodle.net/mobile/moodlemobile2/ for a demo Regards, Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: use desktop browser to test and view moodle mobile site
ResponsesInList.Text: Bootstrap is a responsive design framework. So it uses CSS media queries to deliver flexible layouts to different devices and screen sizes. Moodle 2.5's Clean theme is based on Bootstrap. (I misremembered this when writing the previous message.) So Clean should resize nicely based on what screen size it is presented with. Device detection works by delivering different themes to different browsers based on their user agent string. If you wanted to use a url to get to a different theme, you have to set this up in config.php and then pass it a query parameter in the URL. It's described at http://docs.moodle.org/22/en/Theme_settings#Session_themes

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Why I can't accept my self-sign server certificate?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, the app accepts the certificates authorities that Android browser accepts, it's not something we can change. We don't have plans for allowing SSL self signed certificates, it's something not compatible with the current app authentication system (we did some research, we cannot allow specific sites in the app for using self signed; The only way will be to allow all the sites the app can connect to use untrusted certificates and this is a major security risk) Cheers, Juan

ResponsesInList.Title: mobile plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I asked already a question about how to add a plugin and I followed these Steps: 1. Enable debugging, Disable all caches (Im not sure what i have to do to disable all caches so please if you can tell me what I have to do) , Enable WebServices in Advanced options, Enable WebServices protocols (REST), Enable Mobile Services (in Plugins -> WebServices-> Services) 2. Find the full source code here: https://github.com/cvaconsulting/moodle-local_custommm 3. Unzip this folder in /moodle/local folder 4. Go to Home > Site administration > Plugins > Web services > External services 5. Add a new external service: custommm for ex. 6. When creating, the flats "Can download files" and "Enabled" must be checked 7. Add the following functions: local_custommm_get_grades local_custommm_update_grade local_custommm_get_forums_by_courses local_custommm_get_forum_discussions local_custommm_get_forum_posts 8. Go to phpMyAdmin /yourdatabase/ mdl_external_services table and add manually a shortname for the new Service 9. Edit the config.json file and change the wsservice parameter in order to point to the shortname of the Service you created before: "wsservice" : ["moodle_mobile_app", "custommm"], 10. ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, the permission is not for making phone calls, are for read/write the call log see: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.moodle.moodlemobile&hl=en In any case we don't read/write the phone call log, it seems an issue in Android, see: http://developer.android.com/reference/android/Manifest.permission.html#READ_CALL_LOG Note: If your app uses the `READ_CONTACTS` permission and both your `minSdkVersion` and `targetSdkVersion` values are set to 15 or lower, the system implicitly grants your app this permission. If you don't need this permission, be sure your `targetSdkVersion` is 16 or higher. We will try to fix that for the next release/version Version 1.6 can access: Identity find accounts on the device Contacts/Calendar read your contacts modify your contacts Phone read call log write call log Photos/Media/Files modify or delete the contents of your USB storage test access to protected storage Camera/Microphone record audio Other receive data from Internet full network access view network connections change your audio settings prevent device from sleeping control vibration

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: MyMobile vs. Moodle Mobile
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Jay, MyMobile and Moodle Mobile are not alternate solutions for Moodle Mobile access. You have to think that are complementary tools: - MyMobile is a Moodle theme that enable any user to browse a full Moodle installation - Moodle Mobile is a mobile app that enable users to read offline contents, use their Mobile phone hardware (camera, audio recorder) and also in a near future receive notifications. Moodle Mobile will never have the 100% of Moodle features, this will required a big developers team. Moodle Mobile is just a mobile app that may help users to read offline contents and receive notifications. By the way, MyMobile theme doesn't work very well, Moodle HQ is creating a new theme called bootstrap/simple that will be available in Moodle 2.5 that follows a responsive design approach. It works very well on Mobile. Regards

ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi all! I installed airnotifier in my local Ubuntu 14.04 machine for testing and achieved a fully working installation, tested with iOs and Android. Then I requested an installation in a production linux server and reconfigured all as I did in local, but this time the Android notification are not working (while the iOs notification are still working). When I try to send a broadcast notification Airnotifier crashes with this crashlog: 
```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/lib/python2.6/site-packages/tornado/web.py", line 1077, in _execute
    *self.path_args, **self.path_kwargs)
  File "/usr/lib/python2.6/site-packages/tornado/web.py", line 1892, in wrapper
    return method(self, *args, **kwargs)
  File "/opt/airnotifier-moodle/controllers/site_controller.py", line 275, in post
    gcm = self.gcmconnections[appname][0]
KeyError: u'iuibi_android'
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Airnotifier (moodle branch) working in local net but not in production
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Daniele, Airnotifier support is provided in the project site: https://github.com/airnotifier/airnotifier/issues Note that the support is done by the software maintainer (Dongsheng Cai), there is an upcoming version of Airnotifier with major changes so I think you may wait until September Regards

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Airnotifier (moodle branch) working in local net but not in production
ResponsesInList.Text: Thank you, Juan. BTW , I think it can be a configuration issue rather than a real Airnotifier's issue... I cannot find an Airnotifier support forum for asking this question instead of firing a bug in the Github issues page... Thank you btw.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Airnotifier (moodle branch) working in local net but not in production
ResponsesInList.Text:
Ok, I managed to find the problem. Posting it here in case someone needs it. The problem was the Airnotifier server wasn't restarted after Android GCM configuration. Simply pressing "Save" at the end of the configuration screen is not enough to start the android GCM service. At this point the behaviour is (e.g. when sending a broadcast notification for debug): Apple notification succesfully delivered No GCM notification produced Error shown on screen: 
```text
KeyError: u'MY_PROJECT_NAME'
```
 The solution is to kill the python instance running Airnotifier and then restart it. I think this is a wrong behaviour because there is a button for starting/stopping Apple APNs service, but there isn't an equivalent for Google GCM; so I'm going to open an issue at Airnotifier's GitHub.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Mobile 1.4.4 submitted to Google Play and Apple App Store
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Juan, Many thanks for your help in resolving this issue. The root cause of our issue was as follows: The 'login/token.php' script uses the 'required_param' function to retrieve the username and password provided by the user. If either of these parameters are not provided a 'moodle_exception' is thrown. We have modified our Moodle code base so that when a moodle_exception is thrown a '500 Internal Server Error' status code is returned. After all, an exception has just occurred. To fix the issue, I have implemented a check in the 'login/token.php' file which looks at the request method and the user agent string. If the request method is a 'HEAD' request, and the user agent string matches a set of criteria, a '200 OK' status code is returned. This allows the site check by the Moodle Mobile app to succeed and the username and password fields to be displayed. With thanks. -Corey

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Mobile App
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes David, I agree with you, for that reason we have changed our current approach of how to implement WS/new features for the app: Here you have the rationale: The current Mobile app is just a Web Services client/consumer that depends on the web service functions available in the remote Moodle Old Moodle versions only provides a very basic functionality, modern versions like 2.7 provides new webservices for Push notifications, grades, forums, assignments, etc... This causes some problems: - Administrator need to have their Moodle installation upgraded to the last stable version in order to allow users to benefit of all the app features (I.e: calendar events are only displayed for sites Moodle 2.6 and above, Push notifications require 2.6 at least) - We have to create new webservices in the core and wait to be integrated in major releases, or minor releases (but just in current stable) This makes the development process slow - The app seems to be very simple and limited for most users in a first look (in older Moodle versions). New approach: Create a new add-one (local_mobile) that provides additional features for Moodle version starting 2.4. This new add-one will have functions backported from 2.7 to 2.4, 2.5, 2.6 etc... The add-one will be available for download in the moodle.org/plugins directory, once installed in a Moodle site it will create automatically a new service mobile_app_ext with all the current and new functions The benefits will be: - If you install the plugin in a 2.4 version, it will provide all the missing functionality available in 2.7, so the users of the Mobile app will be able to use all the functionalities available in the app. - We can easily add new functions in that add-one without having to wait for major releases or minor current stable releases - Contributors can create new webservices to be integrated in this add-one - For administrators it's easier to update plugins instead the whole Moodle site - We can use that plugin for adding additional functionalities, like the CAS/ Shibboleth support The only disadvantage of this approach is that it will require to install an add-one to your Moodle site, but the benefits are huge. Notice that if you don't install the plugin the Mobile app will still work but with limited functionalities

I was able to solve my " we lost connection, you need to reconnect. Your token is now invalid" problem. There was several questions... I was not changing the wsservice paran in the config.json I just added one function (local_custommm_get_grades) in the new "custommm" external service and is required to add all the functions Moodle include in the prebuilt "Moodle mobile web service" because we are not going to use this one. Finally the column shortname is been inserted with a null value when I create a new Custom External Webservice. Moodle does not display this value and it is required to know it to update the "wssservice" (config.json) param. Now you can solve it updating the column on the database. 
```text
update mdl_external_services set shortname='custommm' where name='custommm';
```
 I think the last problem is a bug but I don't find nothing related on the bug trucker. Can you reproduce it?

ResponsesInList.Title: Moody - Moodle web client for Android
ResponsesInList.Text: Moody will be our main access to the Moodle e-learning platform, but it was also thought to be our best friend, the one who will help us with every school matter. The desired idea is Moody to be known as a friend and not a resource. Therefore, it will have access to the Moodle content, show us the information in a user friendly environment and notify about new developments in our important and favorite subjects. Features Native Android application Open source UI themes and completely customizable Free Access to courses while offline Requirements Moodle >= 2.2 Android >= 3.0.x Internet connection How it works The client sends a user name and password to the web service login script. The script returns a token for that user account. The client calls a particular web service function on a protocol server including the token . The protocol server uses the token to check that the user can call the function. The protocol server call the matching external function, located in a externallib.php file inside the relevant module. The external function checks that the current user has_capability to do this operation. The external function calls the matching Moodle core function (in lib.php usually). The core function can return a result to the external function. The external function will return a result to the protocol server. The protocol server returns the result to the client. What Moody can do Moody is able to get all the contents of your courses Notify you about new contents in your favorites Add your courses to your favorites Get the latest contents from all of your courses Search in your courses Send messages to contacts Edit profile picture Download : https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.firetrap.moody&hl=pt_PT Project page: http://firetrap.github.io/Moody/#!index.md

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moody - Moodle web client for Android
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey Fábio, From what you have posted here and on your website this looks like quite a neat implementation of moodle on a mobile - certainly looks visually nice and has some nice features. A couple of questions though; How similar is it to the 'official' moodle mobile apps? is it a fork or a completely different project? How do you see this project developing? The notifications element really appeals to me (and is somthing we are asked about quite frequently) - how does this operate? does it work when the app is not open? Thanks in advance! Cheers Mark

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moody - Moodle web client for Android
ResponsesInList.Text: Moody it's a independent project, isn't a fork from the official ,it uses a open source communication library with REST protocol to interact with Moodle servers ( https://github.com/firetrap/MoodyRest ).  The main differences between official app and Moody are: offline access,  push notifications, the option to send messages. The next update will bring some new features and raise the quality and add more stability to the app. The development it's done by me and with some help from Bill Antónia in the REST library. The development it's always dependent with Moodle. Moody in contrary with the official app it needs that a service is created in the server side. Why it is this needed? Because the default web service already pre-built in Moodle only have a few functions and Moody needs more like send messages get user profile picture etc etc. It's a win-win if Moodle enable all the functions in the default web service but at the moment it's not activated so i need "moody_service" (Moody service it's a service created inside moodle with functions available in Moodle, it will never install outside content). Yes the notifications works when the app it's not open, the notifications it's an android service wich is running in background, with a time defined in the settings the service it will check with Moodle server if exists new contents in the courses, if exists it will send a notification to the user about the new content. Thanks, Fábio Barreiros - Moody founder.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, the Push notification (that will be in core for 2.7, in 2.6 is a contributed plugin) system is connected to the messages/notification system in Moodle. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Proposed New Functionality
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David, Totara LMS is a custom distribution of Moodle, not a plugin. They are developing a mobile app based on MoodleMobile. The idea is join efforts so MoodleMobile can benefit from new features added in the Totara app that are not specific for Totara LMS Regarding the future of Moodle Mobile, I can assure you that we have a long roadmap for MoodleMobile app, I was talking in person with Martin Dougiamas last week, also here is the presentation I did with Martin Dougiamas a few days ago in the MoodleMoot Spain. Things like responsive themes are described: http://www.slideshare.net/juanleyva/moodlemoot-spain-2013-juan-leyva-martin-dougiamas-on-moodle-mobile-1 Regards

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Proposed New Functionality
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David, To add to Juan's reply: No you don't need Totara to make use of most of these.  As mentioned Totara is a distribution of Moodle, but all the work we are doing that can be used directly with Moodle i.e. the non Totara specific functionality, is being incorporated into the Moodle Mobile code for use by the Moodle community.  The additional Totara specific functionality will be part of the Totara distribution code base. Everything in section 4.2 is Moodle specific and should be included in future Moodle Mobile releases.  Section 4.3 is the work that ties into Totara functionality. This work should not be impacted by MNet changes as we are linking into Moodle webservices for all functionality. The minimum version of Moodle will probably be 2.6 but it may be that it will work on 2.5.  We need to get it working on 2.5 for Totara as the Totara code base is one version behind the current Moodle release and hopefully the work we will do will be easily backportable/compatible with 2.5. re opening word files, we are saying that we are not going to handle file formats within the Moodle app, we are going to rely on third party readers installed on the phone to handle opening these Regards David

ResponsesInList.Title: MAJOR NEWS: Change in our Moodle mobile app strategy
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, After much thought and various events over the past 6 months I've come to a major change in how Moodle HQ will be supporting mobile development for Moodle. The current way we were doing it was inefficient.  It was costing a lot, not moving very fast and not serving our community in the best way possible. So in a nutshell, we are doing this: We are dropping development of the official iOS app "My Moodle" written in Objective-C (although the app will continue to be available in the app store and will continue working for quite some time yet) We are releasing the code for it under the GPL: https://github.com/moodlehq/mymoodle and you are very free to build your own custom apps from it or use the code in other projects (just be careful with the Moodle trademark ). Instead we have contracted Juan Leyva from Moodle Partner CV&A Consulting to lead development of his HTML5+Phonegap app (currently called Unofficial Moodle Mobile ).  The new app will be called ' Moodle Mobile '.  Supported by Jerome from Moodle HQ and others we have a roadmap to turn it into a solution for all platforms simultaneously.   The new design will continue using standard Moodle REST web services , be highly modular, and allow a lot of you to contribute to development.  See the roadmap here: MOBILE-153 . The new app will continue to be licensed under the GPL and you are also allowed to fork it and build your own custom apps if you wish.   (I think a lot of institutions would like to have an app that is hardwired for their own installation and includes other info specific to their institution). Our target is to release first official versions of this new app for iOS, Android and possibly others around the time of Moodle 2.4 at the end of this year. I hope you all like this news!   Although we will lose a little speed and smoothness in the interface when moving to HTML5, I think the idea of building up community effort around a cross-platform mobile client will far outweigh that and sets us up better for the long term. Cheers!
